phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Mĩm-Ṣãd
phrases.explanation: Early commentators offered several explanations for these opening letters: some took them as an oath by Allah’s names, others saw each letter as standing for attributes such as Allah the All-Knowing, the Truthful, and the Creator, while others held that they represent abbreviated divine names, letters of the alphabet, or a symbolic allusion to the numerical span of nations.

phrases.translation: ˹This is˺ a Book sent down to you ˹O Prophet˺
phrases.explanation: Allah addresses the Prophet Muhammad to affirm that this Quran is a revealed Scripture sent down to him from his Lord, just as earlier scriptures were sent down to the messengers who came before him, establishing his prophethood and message with undeniable divine authority before all humanity.

phrases.translation: —do not let anxiety into your heart regarding it—
phrases.explanation: Allah forbids His Messenger from feeling any tightness, doubt, or heaviness in his chest when conveying this Book out of fear that the polytheists will reject or oppose him, commanding him instead to proclaim it boldly and bear their hostility patiently as previous messengers did.

phrases.translation: so with it you may warn ˹the disbelievers˺, and as a reminder to the believers
phrases.explanation: The Quran was revealed for a twofold purpose: so that the Prophet might warn the disbelievers of the painful punishment awaiting those who reject Allah’s signs, and so that it might serve as a clear reminder, admonition, and source of mindfulness for those who believe in its truth.

phrases.translation: Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and do not take others as guardians besides Him.
phrases.explanation: Addressing the people of Quraysh and all humanity, Allah commands them to follow the revelation sent down to them from their Lord in the Quran and forbids taking devils, idols, or false leaders as patrons and helpers whose commands they obey in defiance of Allah.

phrases.translation: How seldom are you mindful
phrases.explanation: Allah concludes with a stern rebuke to the disbelievers, pointing out that despite the clarity of His revelation and His warnings against false patrons, only rarely do they reflect upon His message, take admonition to heart, or step back from the error in which they persist.

phrases.translation: ˹Imagine˺ how many societies We have destroyed!
phrases.explanation: Warning the Meccan polytheists against persisting in their denial of the Prophet, Allah reminds them of the many rebellious towns and nations He destroyed in past ages when they rejected the messengers sent to them and stubbornly disobeyed their Lord’s commands despite receiving clear proofs.

phrases.translation: Our torment took them by surprise ˹while sleeping˺ at night or midday
phrases.explanation: Allah’s overwhelming punishment struck those disobedient communities suddenly at the very hours when they felt safest and most heedless, overtaking some of them by night while they lay asleep in their beds and others in the bright midday while they rested comfortably in their homes.

phrases.translation: Their only cry—when overwhelmed by Our torment—was, “We have indeed been wrongdoers.”
phrases.explanation: When Allah’s inescapable punishment actually descended upon those destroyed communities and they beheld ruin with their own eyes, every false boast vanished and their only cry was to confess that they had wronged their own souls by disobeying Allah, at a moment when regret could no longer save them.

phrases.translation: We will surely question those who received messengers
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection Allah will surely question all the nations and communities to whom messengers were sent, demanding a full account of how they responded to the divine call and whether they obeyed the teachings and revelations brought to them by their prophets.

phrases.translation: and We will question the messengers ˹themselves˺
phrases.explanation: Allah will likewise question the messengers themselves on that Day in the presence of their nations regarding whether they faithfully conveyed the messages entrusted to them by their Lord, and how their respective communities answered their call to pure monotheism and sincere obedience to Allah alone.

phrases.translation: Then We will give them a full account with sure knowledge
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Judgment Allah will recount to both the messengers and their nations everything they did and said during their worldly lives, setting forth their complete record on the basis of His unerring, all-encompassing knowledge of all their deeds, words, and inward intentions.

phrases.translation: —for We were never absent
phrases.explanation: Nothing of their words or actions in the world could ever escape that final reckoning or be concealed from their Lord, because Allah was never absent from His servants at any moment when they acted or spoke, whether in secret or in public before others.

phrases.translation: The weighing on that Day will be just.
phrases.explanation: The weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection will be conducted with complete truth, justice, and equity, so that no soul is wronged in the least by having a good deed diminished or an uncommitted sin added to its account before Allah on that Day.

phrases.translation: As for those whose scale will be heavy ˹with good deeds˺, ˹only˺ they will be successful
phrases.explanation: Those whose scales are heavy with faith and righteous deeds, weighted down as early commentators explain by the testimony that there is no god except Allah, are the ones who will attain deliverance from the Fire and everlasting success in the lofty gardens of Paradise.

phrases.translation: But those whose scale is light, they have doomed themselves
phrases.explanation: In contrast, those whose scales are light on the Day of Resurrection because they lacked faith and righteous deeds will have ruined their own souls and forfeited their share of Allah’s mercy, consigning themselves to eternal loss, disgrace, and unending misery in the depths of Hellfire.

phrases.translation: for wrongfully denying Our signs
phrases.explanation: They brought that ruin and eternal loss upon their own souls because during their worldly lives they unjustly rejected Allah’s revealed signs and miraculous proofs out of stubborn arrogance instead of submitting to them in faith and obedience as was rightfully due to their Lord.

phrases.translation: We have indeed established you on earth and provided you with a means of livelihood.
phrases.explanation: Reminding the children of Adam of His abundant blessings upon them, Allah recalls how He gave them settled dwellings and authority on the earth and provided them with crops, livestock, trade, and every means of sustenance by which they maintain their lives from generation to generation.

phrases.translation: ˹Yet˺ you seldom give any thanks
phrases.explanation: Despite enjoying these countless habitations, bounties, and means of livelihood granted to them by their Creator, human beings only rarely show true gratitude to their Lord in word and deed by acknowledging His blessings, worshipping Him alone without partner, and obeying His commands in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Surely We created you, then shaped you, then said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,”
phrases.explanation: As early commentators explain, Allah first created and fashioned their father Adam in his bodily form, or created Adam and formed his descendants in their mothers’ wombs, and then commanded His angels to prostrate before Adam in a gesture of honour, greeting, and salute rather than worship.

phrases.translation: so they all did—but not Iblîs, who refused to prostrate with the others
phrases.explanation: All the angels immediately obeyed their Lord’s command and prostrated before Adam together in humble submission, except Iblis, who was present among them yet arrogantly refused out of pride and envy to join those who prostrated before Adam and thus openly rebelled against Allah’s command.

phrases.translation: Allah asked, “What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?”
phrases.explanation: Rebuking Iblis for his open defiance of the divine command, Allah asked him before the assembly of angels what had prevented him and held him back from prostrating before Adam when his Creator and Sovereign Lord had directly ordered him to do so in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: He replied, “I am better than he is: You created me from fire and him from clay.”
phrases.explanation: Driven by envy and false pride, Iblis answered that he was superior in origin and substance to Adam and therefore ought not to bow before him, boasting that Allah had created him from blazing fire whereas He had created Adam from lowly clay and mud.

phrases.translation: Allah said, “Then get down from Paradise! It is not for you to be arrogant here.
phrases.explanation: Because of his insolent rebellion, Allah commanded Iblis to descend from the heavens and Paradise, declaring that no creature dwelling in the noble realm of the angels is ever permitted to act arrogantly against Allah’s command or refuse obedience to His sovereign decree in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: So get out! You are truly one of the disgraced.”
phrases.explanation: Allah ordered Iblis to depart from that lofty, blessed station at once without delay, condemning him to be among the abased, humiliated, and despised creatures in both worlds on account of his haughty refusal to obey his Lord’s command in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: He appealed, “Then delay my end until the Day of their resurrection.”
phrases.explanation: When Allah expelled him from heaven in disgrace, Iblis asked his Lord to grant him respite and delay his end until the Day when mankind will be resurrected from their graves, hoping thereby to escape death altogether since there is no death after the resurrection.

phrases.translation: Allah said, “You are delayed ˹until the appointed Day˺.”
phrases.explanation: Allah answered that Iblis was indeed among those granted respite, though as clarified elsewhere in the Quran only until the appointed Day of the first blast of the Trumpet when all creatures die, rather than sparing him from tasting death altogether as he had hoped.

phrases.translation: He said, “For leaving me to stray
phrases.explanation: Once assured that his life would be prolonged until the appointed time, Iblis swore that because Allah had decreed his misguidance and downfall when he refused to prostrate before Adam, he would spend his respite seeking revenge against Adam and all his descendants in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: I will lie in ambush for them on Your Straight Path
phrases.explanation: Iblis vowed to lie in ambush for the children of Adam along Allah’s straight path, which early commentators explain as the true religion of Islam and obedience that leads to Paradise, striving with all his might to bar them from following it and to lead them astray.

phrases.translation: I will approach them from their front, their back, their right, their left,
phrases.explanation: Expounding his threat, Iblis declared that he would assail human beings from every direction: from their front by casting doubt on the hereafter, from their back by making this world alluring, and from their right and left by corrupting their good deeds and beautifying sins.

phrases.translation: and then You will find most of them ungrateful.”
phrases.explanation: Through this relentless temptation from every side, Iblis boasted, speaking from his own conjecture and wishful thinking, that Allah would find most of Adam’s descendants ungrateful and disobedient rather than thankful monotheists who acknowledge His blessings, worship Him alone, and obey His messengers in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Allah said, “Get out of Paradise! You are disgraced and rejected!
phrases.explanation: Allah commanded Iblis to depart from Paradise despised as a blameworthy rebel who deserves every reproach from his Creator and from all creation, and banished as an accursed outcast driven far away from Allah’s mercy, honour, and every form of good in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: I will certainly fill up Hell with you and your followers all together.”
phrases.explanation: Allah then swore a solemn oath that He would surely fill Hell with Iblis and with all among the children of Adam and the jinn who follow him in idolatry, error, and disobedience instead of obeying their Lord and His messengers in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: ˹Allah said,˺ “O Adam! Live with your wife in Paradise and eat from wherever you please,
phrases.explanation: After banishing Iblis from heaven, Allah invited Adam and his wife Eve to dwell together in the Garden of Paradise and to eat freely, comfortably, and abundantly of its pleasant fruits from wherever they wished in the Garden without hardship or restriction in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: but do not approach this tree, or else you will be wrongdoers.”
phrases.explanation: As a single test of obedience amidst that vast abundance, Allah forbade Adam and Eve from approaching and eating from one specific tree in the Garden, warning them that if they transgressed His prohibition they would become wrongdoers against their own souls in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Then Satan tempted them in order to expose what was hidden of their nakedness.
phrases.explanation: Satan then whispered insidious suggestions to Adam and Eve, speaking to them directly or from within the serpent’s mouth according to early reports, in order to strip them of their covering of light and expose their hidden private parts to each other in shame in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: He said, “Your Lord has forbidden this tree to you only to prevent you from becoming angels or immortals.”
phrases.explanation: To entice them into eating from the forbidden tree, Satan lied to them by claiming that their Lord had barred them from it only to prevent them from becoming angels who know good and evil or immortals who dwell in Paradise forever without tasting death.

phrases.translation: And he swore to them, “I am truly your sincere advisor.”
phrases.explanation: To overcome their hesitation, Satan swore a solemn oath by Allah to Adam and Eve that he was a sincere adviser to them in urging them to eat from the tree, deceiving them because a believer does not expect anyone to swear falsely by Allah.

phrases.translation: So he brought about their fall through deception.
phrases.explanation: By swearing falsely in Allah’s name that he wished them well and was a sincere counselor to them, Satan lured Adam and Eve down from their high station of obedience into slipping and committing the forbidden act through his treacherous deceit in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: And when they tasted of the tree, their nakedness was exposed to them, prompting them to cover themselves with leaves from Paradise.
phrases.explanation: The moment they tasted of the tree, the luminous garment of nail-like light that had clothed them fell away, exposing their private parts to each other for the first time so that they hurried in shame to stitch fig leaves of Paradise over their bodies.

phrases.translation: Then their Lord called out to them, “Did I not forbid you from that tree and ˹did I not˺ tell you that Satan is your sworn enemy?”
phrases.explanation: Their Lord then called out to Adam and Eve in gentle reproach as they sought to cover themselves with leaves, asking why they had eaten when He had expressly forbidden them that tree and warned them beforehand that Satan was their open, declared enemy in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: They replied, “Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves.
phrases.explanation: Unlike Iblis who persisted in arrogance and blamed his Lord for his downfall, Adam and Eve immediately confessed their sin before Allah in humility and remorse, acknowledging that by disobeying His command they had wronged their own souls and stood in need of His pardon.

phrases.translation: If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will certainly be losers.”
phrases.explanation: Using the words of repentance that Allah inspired in them, Adam and Eve pleaded that unless their Lord forgave their transgression by covering it and encompassed them with His mercy, they would surely be among those who perish in eternal loss and ruin in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Allah said, “Descend as enemies to each other.
phrases.explanation: Allah commanded Adam, Eve, and Iblis, along with the serpent according to several early reports, to descend from heaven to the earth as mutual adversaries, with Satan and human beings locked in ongoing enmity, hostility, and struggle against one another in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: You will find in the earth a residence and provision for your appointed stay.”
phrases.explanation: Allah decreed that upon the earth they and their offspring would have a place of settlement and a temporary enjoyment of livelihood until the end of their appointed lifespans and the coming of the Final Hour when this world passes away in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: He added, “There you will live, there you will die,
phrases.explanation: Addressing Adam, Eve, and their progeny, Allah decreed that upon the earth they would spend the days of their worldly lives in toil and trial, and upon it they would taste death and be buried in their graves when their appointed terms expired in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: and from there you will be resurrected.”
phrases.explanation: From their graves in that very same earth Allah will bring them all forth alive again on the Day of Resurrection to stand before Him for judgment and receive the full, just recompense of the deeds they performed during their lives in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: O children of Adam! We have provided for you clothing to cover your nakedness and as an adornment.
phrases.explanation: Addressing the Arab polytheists who used to circumambulate the Kaaba naked as well as all humanity, Allah reminds them of His favour in sending down physical garments to conceal their shameful parts from others and fine attire to adorn their bodies in dignity in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: However, the best clothing is righteousness.
phrases.explanation: Yet superior to any outward garment of cloth is the clothing of righteousness, explained by early commentators as faith, reverent fear of Allah, modest shame, and righteous action, which adorns the heart and protects the believer from disgrace in both worlds in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: This is one of Allah’s bounties, so perhaps you will be mindful
phrases.explanation: These blessings of physical clothing and spiritual guidance are among the signs and favours of Allah’s grace toward humanity, granted so that people may remember His kindness, reflect on His mercy, and obey His commands instead of following shameful pagan customs in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: O children of Adam! Do not let Satan deceive you as he tempted your parents out of Paradise and caused their cover to be removed in order to expose their nakedness.
phrases.explanation: Allah warns all descendants of Adam not to let Satan seduce them into idolatry or shameful practices such as naked circumambulation, just as he deceived their parents Adam and Eve and caused them to be expelled from Paradise with their covering stripped away in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Surely he and his soldiers watch you from where you cannot see them.
phrases.explanation: Human beings must remain constantly vigilant against Satan’s temptations and seek refuge in Allah at all times, because Iblis and his host of jinn and devils watch human beings from where humans cannot see them or perceive their hidden approach in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: We have made the devils allies of those who disbelieve
phrases.explanation: As for those who reject faith in Allah and refuse His guidance, Allah has made the devils their patrons, allies, and close companions who incite them to disobedience and lead them ever deeper into error, sin, and ultimate ruin in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Whenever they commit a shameful deed, they say, “We found our forefathers doing it and Allah has commanded us to do it.”
phrases.explanation: When the pagan Arabs committed shameful acts, especially circumambulating the Kaaba naked while claiming they should not perform tawaf in clothes in which they had sinned, they excused themselves by saying they were following their forefathers and that Allah had commanded it in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Say, “No! Allah never commands what is shameful. How can you attribute to Allah what you do not know?”
phrases.explanation: Allah instructs His Messenger to refute their slander by declaring that Allah never commands shameless indecency or disobedience to Him, and by rebuking them for fabricating falsehoods against Allah and attributing invented laws, taboos, and rites to Him without any knowledge, revelation, or proof. Their claim that custom equals divine command is exposed as a baseless lie against their Creator.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “My Lord has commanded uprightness and dedication ˹to Him alone˺ in worship, calling upon Him with sincere devotion.
phrases.explanation: Instead of shameful innovations, Allah has commanded justice and fairness, embodied in the testimony that there is no god except Allah, and directed believers to orient themselves rightly in every place and time of prayer, calling upon Him with pure monotheistic devotion in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Just as He first brought you into being, you will be brought to life again.”
phrases.explanation: Just as Allah originated human beings from nothing when they did not exist, He will surely bring them back to life on the Day of Resurrection to judge each soul according to the faith or disbelief upon which it was created and died in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: He has guided some, while others are destined to stray.
phrases.explanation: In the hereafter and in this world, humanity is divided into two groups upon whom Allah’s prior decree is fulfilled: one group whom Allah has guided to faith and salvation, and another group upon whom misguidance and ruin have justly taken effect in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: They have taken devils as their masters instead of Allah—thinking they are ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: Those upon whom misguidance became due went astray because they took the devils as their masters and obeyed their whisperings instead of Allah, all while deluding themselves that their idolatrous practices were right guidance and the path of truth in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: O Children of Adam! Dress properly whenever you are at worship.
phrases.explanation: Revealed concerning pagan tribes who circled the Kaaba naked and forbade wearing clothes during pilgrimage, this verse commands believers to wear proper clothing that covers their private parts and adorns them decently at every mosque and every time of prayer in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Eat and drink, but do not waste.
phrases.explanation: Allah also permits His servants to eat and drink freely of the wholesome foods, meats, and drinks He has created for their nourishment, while forbidding them to transgress proper bounds by declaring lawful foods unlawful or consuming what Allah has prohibited, since Allah never loves those who overstep His limits.

phrases.translation: Surely He does not like the wasteful
phrases.explanation: Allah concludes with a warning that He does not love those who exceed the limits He has ordained, whether by inventing unauthorized prohibitions in religion, wasting wealth in sin, or indulging in what He has forbidden to His servants in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Ask, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Who has forbidden the adornments and lawful provisions Allah has brought forth for His servants?”
phrases.explanation: Allah instructs the Prophet to challenge the polytheists who invented arbitrary taboos against wearing garments during tawaf or eating certain meats and fats, asking who had any authority to forbid the clothing and wholesome provisions Allah brought forth for His servants in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Say, “They are for the enjoyment of the believers in this worldly life, but they will be exclusively theirs on the Day of Judgment.
phrases.explanation: Although disbelievers share with believers in enjoying these worldly blessings of clothing and food during this earthly life, on the Day of Resurrection all pure provisions and adornments will belong exclusively to the believers in Paradise, with no share for disbelievers in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: This is how We make Our revelations clear for people of knowledge.”
phrases.explanation: Just as He has clarified the rulings on lawful clothing and wholesome food in these verses, Allah sets forth His revelations and proofs in detail for people of knowledge who reflect on His signs and recognize the truth of His commands in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Say, “My Lord has only forbidden open and secret indecencies, sinfulness, unjust aggression,
phrases.explanation: Refuting the polytheists’ invented taboos, the Prophet is commanded to declare what Allah has truly forbidden: shameful deeds committed openly or in secret, every form of sin against Allah’s commands, and wrongful insolence and transgression against truth and people’s rights in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: associating ˹others˺ with Allah ˹in worship˺—a practice He has never authorized—and attributing to Allah what you do not know.”
phrases.explanation: Above all else, Allah has forbidden associating partners with Him in worship without any proof, warrant, or authority ever sent down from Him, and fabricating lies against Allah by claiming without knowledge that He forbade lawful provisions or commanded shameful idolatrous rites. Joining idol worship to invented religious laws is therefore the gravest form of transgression against Allah.

phrases.translation: For each community there is an appointed term.
phrases.explanation: Warning the polytheists who persist in disbelief and invented falsehoods, Allah declares that for every nation and generation He has decreed a fixed lifespan and an appointed term for their death or the descent of their inescapable punishment in this world. Human impatience cannot alter the timetable Allah has set for the rise and fall of communities.

phrases.translation: When their time arrives, they can neither delay it for a moment, nor could they advance it
phrases.explanation: Once that decreed hour of destruction or death arrives for a community, they have no power to postpone it by even a single moment so as to repent, nor can it ever come before its appointed time in Allah’s decree in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: O children of Adam! When messengers from among yourselves come to you reciting My revelations
phrases.explanation: Renewing the covenant given when humanity was sent down from the Garden to earth, Allah addresses all descendants of Adam regarding the human messengers He sends from among their own kind to recite His revelations to them and clarify His commands, laws, and prohibitions. This guidance gives every generation the opportunity to know what pleases their Lord before judgment arrives.

phrases.translation: —whoever shuns evil and mends their ways, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve
phrases.explanation: Whoever responds to those messengers by fearing Allah, avoiding idolatry and major sins, and reforming his conduct through sincere faith and obedience will have no fear when facing the terrors of the hereafter, nor will he grieve over whatever he left behind in the worldly life.

phrases.translation: But those who receive Our revelations with denial and arrogance will be the residents of the Fire.
phrases.explanation: In contrast to the God-fearing, those who reject Allah’s signs and messengers as false and arrogantly disdain submitting to His commands will be the companions of the blazing Fire on the Day of Resurrection, reaping the fruit of their rebellion in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: They will be there forever
phrases.explanation: They will abide in that Fire eternally without end, neither dying so as to find relief from its torment nor ever being brought out of its flames, as a just and everlasting requital for their pride and denial of Allah’s truth in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Who does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah or deny His revelations?
phrases.explanation: No one commits greater injustice against himself than the person who invents lies against Allah by attributing false laws and partners to Him, or who denies the revelations and messengers He has sent with clear proofs to guide humanity in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: They will receive what is destined for them, until Our messenger-angels arrive to take their souls, asking them, “Where are those ˹false gods˺ you used to invoke besides Allah?”
phrases.explanation: Such wrongdoers will receive their decreed share of livelihood, lifespan, or predetermined misery in this world until the angel of death and his assistants come to take their souls and rebuke them by asking where the idols they worshipped beside Allah are now to save them.

phrases.translation: They will cry, “They have failed us,”
phrases.explanation: At that moment of death, when every false hope collapses before their eyes, the polytheists will cry out in despair that the false gods they used to invoke have vanished from them and abandoned them without any help or deliverance in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: and they will confess against themselves that they were indeed disbelievers
phrases.explanation: Stripped of every excuse when the angels of death confront them, they will bear witness against their own souls and confess at the moment of death that throughout their worldly lives they had indeed been disbelievers who denied Allah’s truth and worshipped powerless idols beside Him.

phrases.translation: Allah will say, “Enter the Fire along with the ˹evil˺ groups of jinn and humans that preceded you.”
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Judgment Allah will command these polytheists to enter the depths of Hellfire in utter humiliation alongside the bygone generations and communities of disbelieving jinn and humans who walked the very same path of error, rebellion, and idolatry before them. Shared rebellion in the world leads to shared disgrace in the hereafter regardless of social rank.

phrases.translation: Whenever a group enters Hell, it will curse the preceding one
phrases.explanation: Every time a nation of followers enters the Fire, it will curse its sister nation of predecessors and leaders whose example led it astray into idolatry, as each faithless faction disowns and reviles the others inside the flames of Hell in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: until they are all gathered inside, the followers will say about their leaders, “Our Lord! They have misled us, so multiply their torment in the Fire.”
phrases.explanation: Once the earlier leaders and later followers have all been amassed together in the depths of Hell, the lowly followers will point to the chiefs who misled them from the straight path and beg Allah to give them a double punishment of Fire in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: He will answer, “It has already been multiplied for all, but you do not know.”
phrases.explanation: Allah will reply to both groups that for the misleading leaders and the blind followers alike there is already a doubled, manifold torment in the blazing Fire, though neither party realizes the full intensity of the agonizing punishment that the other is enduring. Neither the corrupters nor the corrupted gain any relief from blaming one another inside the Fire.

phrases.translation: Then the leaders will say to their followers, “You were no better than us!
phrases.explanation: Answering their followers’ curses inside Hell, the leaders of disbelief will tell the last of those who followed them that they possessed no superiority, merit, or valid excuse over them, since both groups alike willfully chose disbelief and error over divine guidance. Following influential figures never excuses a person from answering for willful rejection of the truth.

phrases.translation: So taste the torment for what you used to commit.”
phrases.explanation: The leaders, or Allah addressing both groups together in rebuke, will tell them to taste the painful punishment of the Fire in just recompense for the sins, rebellion, and idolatry they used to commit during their lives in the world in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Surely those who receive our revelations with denial and arrogance, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them,
phrases.explanation: For those who deny Allah’s verses and arrogantly spurn obeying them, the gates of heaven are never opened to receive their deeds or prayers during life, nor to admit their wicked souls when angels carry them up after death in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle.
phrases.explanation: Allah declares their entry into the gardens of Paradise to be an absolute impossibility, just as a huge male camel, or on a variant reading a thick braided ship’s cable, can never pass through the tiny eye of an ordinary sewing needle. The vivid proverb underscores that persistent arrogance against revelation closes every door to heavenly mercy.

phrases.translation: This is how We reward the wicked
phrases.explanation: With such utter humiliation, rejection at the gates of heaven, and eternal exclusion from the bliss of Paradise does Allah requite the wicked criminals who persisted in stubborn disbelief and arrogance against His clear signs and sent messengers. Worldly pride before Allah’s signs thus ends in permanent banishment from the realm of honour.

phrases.translation: Hell will be their bed; flames will be their cover.
phrases.explanation: In the depths of Hell the disbelievers will have a couch of blazing fire spread beneath them as their resting place and thick coverings of fire folded over them from above, surrounding them completely on every side with inescapable heat and suffocation. What ordinarily brings rest and shelter in the world becomes an instrument of punishment in Hell.

phrases.translation: This is how We reward the wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: Such encompassing torment of fire from beneath their feet and above their heads is the just recompense with which Allah rewards the wrongdoers who wronged their own souls by worshipping lifeless idols and defying their Lord throughout their earthly lives. The punishment matches their deliberate choice to surround their lives with disobedience and false worship.

phrases.translation: As for those who believe and do good
phrases.explanation: Turning from the dreadful fate of the wicked to the generous reward of the righteous, Allah describes those who believe in Him and His Messenger with sincere hearts and perform the righteous deeds of obedience He has commanded in His revealed Scripture. True salvation joins inward conviction with outward action rather than relying on empty claims alone.

phrases.translation: —We never require of any soul more than what it can afford—
phrases.explanation: In His boundless mercy and justice toward His servants, Allah reassures believers that He never burdens any soul with religious obligations beyond its capacity and strength to fulfill, requiring of each person only what lies within his ability and reach. Divine law is therefore designed as a path of mercy that human beings can actually live by.

phrases.translation: it is they who will be the residents of Paradise. They will be there forever
phrases.explanation: Those who fulfill what lies within their capacity of sincere faith and obedience to Allah will be the blessed inhabitants of Paradise, dwelling in its gardens forever in everlasting joy without ever tasting death, fatigue, sorrow, or end. Their eternal residence contrasts with the fleeting, anxious pleasures for which disbelievers sold their souls.

phrases.translation: We will remove whatever bitterness they had in their hearts. Rivers will flow under their feet.
phrases.explanation: Before they enter Paradise, Allah will cleanse the believers’ chests of every trace of malice, envy, or resentment they ever harboured against one another in the world, while rivers of pure water, milk, wine, and honey flow beneath their lofty dwellings in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: And they will say, “Praise be to Allah for guiding us to this. We would have never been guided if Allah had not guided us.
phrases.explanation: Seeing the honours prepared for them, the believers will praise Allah for guiding them to the faith and righteous deeds that led to this reward, humbly confessing that they could never have found guidance had Allah not graciously guided them in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth.”
phrases.explanation: Beholding with their own eyes the promised bliss of Paradise and the torment of the wicked in Hell, the believers will testify in gratitude that the messengers sent by their Lord in the world had indeed brought the undeniable truth in every promise. What the prophets had warned and promised unseen in the world now stands verified by sight.

phrases.translation: It will be announced to them, “This is Paradise awarded to you for what you used to do.”
phrases.explanation: A herald will proclaim to them in welcome that this is the Garden of Paradise which they have been made to inherit, including the places forfeited by the disbelievers, because of the faith and good deeds they used to practice in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: The residents of Paradise will call out to the residents of the Fire, “We have certainly found our Lord’s promise to be true. Have you too found your Lord’s promise to be true?”
phrases.explanation: Once settled in their gardens, the people of Paradise will call out across to the people of the Fire, declaring that they have found their Lord’s promise of reward for obedience to be completely true, and asking in rebuke whether the damned have likewise found their Lord’s warning of punishment to be true.

phrases.translation: They will reply, “Yes, we have!”
phrases.explanation: From the midst of the flames, the inhabitants of Hell will confess with bitter regret and humiliation that they too have found every warning of punishment their Lord gave them through His messengers in the world to be completely true in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Then a caller will announce to both, “May Allah’s condemnation be upon the wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: A herald will then proclaim between the two groups, in a clear voice heard by all in Paradise and Hell alike, that Allah’s everlasting curse, wrath, and banishment from mercy rest upon the wrongdoers who rejected faith in Him. This public proclamation seals the verdict between the party of faith and the party of tyranny.

phrases.translation: those who hindered ˹others˺ from Allah’s Way, strived to make it ˹appear˺ crooked,
phrases.explanation: Describing who those cursed wrongdoers are, Allah states that they are the ones who turned people away from His religion and path of guidance and sought to make the straight way appear crooked so that no one would follow it in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: and disbelieved in the Hereafter.”
phrases.explanation: Together with barring others from entering Islam and slandering the path of truth, those wrongdoers persistently denied the resurrection, the reckoning, and the reward and punishment of the hereafter, acting without fear of accountability before their Lord on Judgment Day. Disbelief in the final accountability made it easy for them to corrupt religion for worldly gain.

phrases.translation: There will be a barrier between Paradise and Hell.
phrases.explanation: Between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell stands a sturdy wall and partition, identified elsewhere in the Quran as the barrier with a gate that separates divine mercy on its interior from torment on its exterior in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: And on the heights ˹of that barrier˺ will be people who will recognize ˹the residents of˺ both by their appearance.
phrases.explanation: Upon the crest of that wall, called al-Araf, will stand men whose good and bad deeds were equal, according to most early commentators, awaiting Allah’s final pardon, who recognize the people of Paradise by their radiant faces and the people of Hell by their blackened faces and blue eyes.

phrases.translation: They will call out to the residents of Paradise, “Peace be upon you!”
phrases.explanation: Looking toward the blessed inhabitants of the Garden and recognizing them by the brightness and radiance of their faces, the men standing on the heights of al-Araf will call out to them with the salutation of peace, honour, and security. Even before entering Paradise themselves, they rejoice at the safety granted to the people of faith.

phrases.translation: They will have not yet entered Paradise, but eagerly hope to
phrases.explanation: At the time they offer this greeting, the men on the heights will not yet have entered Paradise themselves because their good and bad deeds were equal, though Allah has placed in their hearts the eager, confident hope that He will soon admit them by His grace.

phrases.translation: When their eyes will turn towards the residents of Hell,
phrases.explanation: When the gaze of those standing on the heights of al-Araf is turned from the people of Paradise toward the companions of the blazing Fire below and they behold their blackened faces and terrifying punishment, they are struck with dread in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: they will pray, “Our Lord! Do not join us with the wrongdoing people.”
phrases.explanation: Filled with dread at that sight, they will immediately cry out in earnest supplication to their Lord, begging Him in humility not to place them in the Fire alongside the wrongdoing people who associated partners with Allah and denied Him in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: Those on the heights will call out to some ˹tyrants in the Fire˺, who they will recognize by their appearance,
phrases.explanation: Looking down into Hell, the men on the heights of al-Araf will call out to specific arrogant chiefs and leaders of disbelief whom they recognize by the distinctive marks of their darkened faces and blue eyes in the Fire in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: saying, “Your large numbers and arrogance are of no use ˹today˺
phrases.explanation: Rebuking those fallen tyrants to their faces, the men on the heights will ask what benefit their amassed wealth, large followings, and haughty refusal to obey Allah have brought them now that they lie helpless and disgraced in the Fire. Every worldly advantage they trusted in instead of Allah has vanished at the moment of need.

phrases.translation: Are these ˹humble believers˺ the ones you swore would never be shown Allah’s mercy?”
phrases.explanation: Pointing to the poor, socially weak believers whom the Meccan chiefs used to mock in the world, the men on the heights will ask the damned tyrants whether these are not the very people whom they once swore Allah would never honour with mercy in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: ˹Finally, those on the heights will be told:˺ “Enter Paradise! There will be no fear for you, nor will you grieve.”
phrases.explanation: Allah will then command the men on the heights of al-Araf, or address the humble believers themselves, to enter Paradise in safety, assuring them that no fear shall ever touch them nor shall they grieve over what they left behind in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: The residents of the Fire will then cry out to the residents of Paradise, “Aid us with some water or any provision Allah has granted you.”
phrases.explanation: Consumed by raging thirst and hunger in Hell, the inhabitants of the Fire will cry out to the people of Paradise, begging them to pour down upon them some water or share any of the food and drink Allah has bestowed on them in accordance with Allah’s just decree.

phrases.translation: They will reply, “Allah has forbidden both to the disbelievers
phrases.explanation: The people of Paradise will answer their desperate plea by declaring that Allah has utterly forbidden both the refreshing water and the wholesome provisions of Paradise to the disbelievers who denied His oneness and rejected His messengers in the world. Those who refused the nourishment of divine guidance in life are denied the provisions of bliss.

phrases.translation: those who took this faith ˹of Islam˺ as mere amusement and play and were deluded by ˹their˺ worldly life.”
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers to whom the food and water of Paradise are forbidden are those who mocked the religion Allah commanded them to follow, treating the call to faith as a subject for sport, amusement, and ridicule while the fleeting comforts and ornaments of worldly life deceived them.

phrases.translation: ˹Allah will say,˺ “Today We will ignore them just as they ignored the coming of this Day of theirs
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection Allah will leave them abandoned in the torment of Hell, hungry and thirsty without any food, drink, or relief, just as they neglected to work and prepare during their worldly lives for meeting this Day of reckoning. Deliberate heedlessness toward revelation is answered by deliberate abandonment when the promised reckoning arrives.

phrases.translation: and for rejecting Our revelations.”
phrases.explanation: Allah will likewise forsake them in everlasting punishment on that Day because throughout their lives in the world they knowingly denied and rejected His clear signs, proofs, and revelations after they had been brought to them by His messengers. Their denial was not innocent ignorance, but a stubborn refusal to accept proofs they could see.

phrases.translation: We have certainly brought them a Book which We explained with knowledge
phrases.explanation: Leaving no excuse for those who neglect the hereafter, Allah swears that He has brought them the Quran, a noble Scripture in which truth is distinguished from falsehood and commands from prohibitions in full detail according to His perfect, all-encompassing knowledge. The revelation therefore leaves no room to claim that Allah’s expectations were left vague or hidden.

phrases.translation: —a guide and mercy for those who believe
phrases.explanation: This detailed Scripture sent down to Muhammad serves as clear guidance to the straight path of truth and a saving mercy from error in this world and punishment in the hereafter specifically for a people who believe in it and act upon its teachings. Those who open their hearts to its message find both direction for conduct and deliverance from ruin.

phrases.translation: Do they only await the fulfilment ˹of its warning˺?
phrases.explanation: Having rejected the Quran and its clear proofs, the polytheists are waiting for nothing except the final outcome and actual realization of its promised warnings, resurrection, and punishment to arrive before their eyes on the Day of Judgment. Delaying belief until the threatened realities appear in plain sight removes the very test of faith.

phrases.translation: The Day it will be fulfilled, those who ignored it before will say, “The messengers of our Lord certainly came with the truth.
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Resurrection when that promised outcome arrives visibly before their eyes, those who neglected to act upon the Book in the world will confess with regret that the messengers of their Lord had indeed brought the undeniable truth. Confession under the compulsion of sight brings no benefit once the time for faith has passed.

phrases.translation: Are there any intercessors who can plead on our behalf? Or can we be sent back so we may do ˹good,˺ unlike what we used to do?”
phrases.explanation: In utter despair they will ask whether they have any intercessors to plead with their Lord to save them from punishment, or whether they can be returned to the worldly life to perform righteous deeds of obedience instead of the idolatry they used to commit.

phrases.translation: They will have certainly ruined themselves, and whatever ˹gods˺ they fabricated will fail them
phrases.explanation: By trading everlasting bliss in the hereafter for worthless, fleeting worldly desires, they will have ruined their own souls and forfeited their share of salvation, and all the false deities they invented beside Allah will have vanished from them. Everything they relied on in place of Allah deserts them when final accountability begins.

phrases.translation: Indeed your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days, then established Himself on the Throne.
phrases.explanation: The true Lord worthy of all worship is Allah alone, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, from Sunday through Friday as early commentators explain, and then rose above the Throne in a manner befitting His majesty and sovereignty. Creation is therefore neither random nor ungoverned, but the deliberate work of one sovereign Lord.

phrases.translation: He makes the day and night overlap in rapid succession.
phrases.explanation: By His omnipotent power He causes the darkness of night to cover the brightness of day, with each pursuing the other swiftly and continuously without pause or delay as the hours of one pass into the hours of the other. The regular alternation of light and darkness testifies daily to the single power directing the cosmos.

phrases.translation: He created the sun, the moon, and the stars—all subjected by His command.
phrases.explanation: He also created the sun, the moon, and the stars, all held in complete subjugation and running in their appointed courses across the sky strictly by His command and decree for the benefit of His servants and the reckoning of time. Celestial bodies that pagan nations worshipped are themselves obedient servants under the command of Allah.

phrases.translation: The creation and the command belong to Him ˹alone˺. Blessed is Allah—Lord of all worlds
phrases.explanation: Unlike helpless idols of stone that neither create nor govern anything at all, both all creation and the irresistible command belong exclusively to Allah, the Blessed and Exalted Sovereign and Lord of all worlds. Because He alone creates and governs the universe, He alone deserves the devotion of His creatures.

phrases.translation: Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly.
phrases.explanation: Believers are commanded to call upon their Lord alone in humble submission and quiet sincerity of heart rather than loud, ostentatious display or hypocrisy, for Allah is near to His servants and hears secret supplication. Quiet humility reflects genuine dependence on Allah, whereas noisy display turns worship into performance.

phrases.translation: Surely He does not like the transgressors
phrases.explanation: Indeed, Allah does not love those who overstep proper bounds in supplication or conduct, whether by shouting boastfully in prayer, asking for what is unlawful, or associating false partners with Him in worship. Proper supplication stays within the etiquette of servitude and the pure monotheism Allah has ordained.

phrases.translation: Do not spread corruption in the land after it has been set in order.
phrases.explanation: People must not spread corruption on the earth through idolatry, shedding innocent blood, and disobeying Allah after He has set the land in order by sending His messengers and establishing His just laws and clear proofs. Moral and spiritual disorder is far more destructive to human society than mere material scarcity.

phrases.translation: And call upon Him with hope and fear.
phrases.explanation: Instead of spreading corruption on earth, servants must call upon their Lord alone in sincere devotion, combining reverent fear of His painful punishment for sin with hopeful longing for His generous reward, pardon, and mercy. Balanced devotion avoids both presumptuous complacency about sin and despair of Allah’s forgiving grace.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah’s mercy is always close to the good-doers
phrases.explanation: Truly, the mercy, pardon, and generous reward of Allah in this world and the hereafter are ever near to the doers of good who obey His commands, shun what He has forbidden, and worship Him sincerely. Pursuing excellence in obedience brings a servant directly within the reach of divine compassion.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who sends the winds ushering in His mercy.
phrases.explanation: Showing His power to revive the dead, Allah declares that He is the One who sends forth the winds, either scattered gently across the sky or as heralds bearing glad tidings according to the two canonical readings, ahead of the mercy of rain. Even the movement of the breeze is directed by Allah as a prelude to sustaining life.

phrases.translation: When they bear heavy clouds, We drive them to a lifeless land and then cause rain to fall, producing every type of fruit.
phrases.explanation: Once those winds carry up clouds heavy with abundant water, Allah drives the clouds to a barren, parched land devoid of vegetation and sends down rain upon it to bring forth every kind of fruit and crop for His creatures. Barren soil that seemed beyond recovery flourishes again as soon as Allah commands the rain.

phrases.translation: Similarly, We will bring the dead to life, so perhaps you will be mindful
phrases.explanation: Just as Allah revives dead, barren earth with rain to produce living plants and fruits, so too will He bring the dead forth alive from their graves on the Day of Resurrection, a clear sign set forth so that people may take heed. Every seasonal revival of the earth rehearses the resurrection that sceptics claimed was impossible.

phrases.translation: The fertile land produces abundantly by the Will of its Lord, whereas the infertile land hardly produces anything.
phrases.explanation: When rain falls, good soil with sweet water brings forth rich, wholesome vegetation readily by its Lord’s permission, whereas foul, salty ground yields only scanty, stunted growth with difficulty. Commentators note this parable also illustrates how pure hearts receive revelation fruitfully while corrupt hearts do not.

phrases.translation: This is how We vary ˹Our˺ lessons to those who are thankful
phrases.explanation: In this way Allah varies and clarifies His signs, parables, and proofs in the Quran for a people who show true gratitude for His blessings by obeying Him and reflecting upon His revelations with receptive hearts. Those who receive Allah’s blessings with thankfulness recognize the moral lessons embedded in the natural world.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people. He said, “O my people! Worship Allah—you have no other god except Him.
phrases.explanation: Beginning a series of prophetic accounts that warn the Meccan polytheists, Allah recalls sending Noah to his people. Noah called them to worship Allah alone in humble obedience and abandon false idols, declaring that no other deity deserves worship beside Him. Every prophetic mission begins with this foundational call to free human devotion from false masters.

phrases.translation: I truly fear for you the torment of a tremendous Day.”
phrases.explanation: Out of sincere compassion for his people, Noah warned them that if they persisted in worshipping idols instead of Allah alone, he truly feared for them the overwhelming punishment of a tremendous Day of affliction and ruin. His warning flowed from genuine concern to save his community before divine patience ran out.

phrases.translation: But the chiefs of his people said, “We surely see that you are clearly misguided.”
phrases.explanation: The assembly of leading men and notables among Noah’s idolatrous people rejected his call to worship Allah alone without partner, telling him that in abandoning their ancestral gods they saw him as someone who had strayed into manifest error far from the path of truth.

phrases.translation: He replied, “O my people! I am not misguided!
phrases.explanation: Noah answered his people’s accusation gently and firmly, assuring them that there was no misguidance, folly, or straying from the path of truth in him at all for calling them away from the worship of lifeless idols. True guidance often looks like error to a society accustomed to inherited falsehood.

phrases.translation: But I am a messenger from the Lord of all worlds
phrases.explanation: Rather than being misguided as his chiefs claimed, Noah declared that he was a true messenger sent to them by the Sovereign Lord and Creator of all worlds to summon them to pure monotheism and obedience. His authority rested not on personal ambition, but on the commission of the universal Creator.

phrases.translation: conveying to you my Lord’s messages and giving you ˹sincere˺ advice.
phrases.explanation: As Allah’s appointed messenger, Noah explained that his duty was to convey his Lord’s messages faithfully to them as commanded and to give his people sincere counsel by warning them against divine wrath and guiding them to salvation. A prophet neither invents the message nor withholds warnings that his audience finds unwelcome.

phrases.translation: And I know from Allah what you do not know
phrases.explanation: He urged them to heed his warning without delay because he knew through Allah’s revelation about the inescapable punishment awaiting unrepentant criminals and the generous reward awaiting believers what his ignorant people did not know. Revelation discloses realities of judgment and mercy that unaided human guesswork cannot reach.

phrases.translation: Do you find it astonishing that a reminder should come to you from your Lord through one of your own, warning you,
phrases.explanation: Because his people objected that he was merely a human being like themselves, Noah asked why they found it strange that an admonition from their Lord should come through a man from among them whom they knew, sent to warn them of Allah’s punishment. Choosing a messenger from their own community made it easier for them to verify his honesty.

phrases.translation: so you may beware and perhaps be shown mercy?”
phrases.explanation: Allah sent that human messenger from among their own kin with a clear warning so that they might fear their Lord by abandoning idolatry and obeying His command, and thereby become worthy of receiving His mercy and escaping destruction. Divine warnings are sent not out of hostility, but to open a path to mercy.

phrases.translation: But they rejected him, so We saved him and those with him in the Ark,
phrases.explanation: Despite centuries of patient warning and call to faith, Noah’s people persisted in calling him a liar, so when Allah’s decree arrived He saved Noah and the small group of believers who followed him aboard the laden Ark. Deliverance belonged to those who trusted the message, even though they were few in number.

phrases.translation: and drowned those who rejected Our signs. They were certainly a blind people
phrases.explanation: At the same time Allah drowned all who rejected His proofs and denied His messenger in the overwhelming waters of the Flood, because their hearts were utterly blind to seeing the truth and taking heed of His signs. Physical sight could not save a community that willfully blinded its heart to clear proofs.

phrases.translation: And to the people of ’Âd We sent their brother Hûd.
phrases.explanation: After destroying Noah’s disbelieving people in the Flood, Allah sent to the ancient Arab tribe of Ad, descendants of Iram son of Sam son of Noah, their fellow tribesman and kinsman Hud as a messenger to call them to truth. Sending a kinsman whose lineage and truthfulness they knew removed any excuse for distrust.

phrases.translation: He said, “O my people! Worship Allah—you have no other god except Him. Will you not then fear Him?”
phrases.explanation: Calling them to the same message of pure monotheism as Noah before him, Hud urged his people to worship Allah alone without any idol beside Him and asked whether they would not fear their Creator’s punishment for idolatry. True mindfulness of Allah begins with abandoning every rival object of devotion beside Him.

phrases.translation: The disbelieving chiefs of his people responded, “We surely see you as a fool,
phrases.explanation: The arrogant notables of Ad who denied Allah’s oneness and rejected His message answered Hud with scorn, declaring that they regarded him as foolish and deluded for abandoning their ancestral religion and the worship of their idols. Worldly elites frequently mistake fidelity to truth for folly when it challenges their customs.

phrases.translation: and we certainly think you are a liar.”
phrases.explanation: Adding insult to their charge of folly, the disbelieving chiefs told Hud that they considered him one of the liars in his claim that Allah had sent him to them as a prophet and messenger. By attacking both his judgment and his honesty, they sought to turn the public against him.

phrases.translation: Hûd replied, “O my people! I am no fool!
phrases.explanation: Hud answered his people with calm dignity, assuring them that there was no foolishness, deficiency of intellect, or departure from truth and sound reason in him at all for calling them to worship their Creator. He answered their abuse without anger, keeping the focus squarely on his prophetic mission.

phrases.translation: But I am a messenger from the Lord of all worlds
phrases.explanation: Far from being foolish, he declared that he was a messenger sent by the Sovereign Lord of all worlds to convey His messages and summon them from the worship of lifeless stones to the worship of Allah alone. The One who created and sustains all worlds has every right to command their exclusive worship.

phrases.translation: conveying to you my Lord’s messages. And I am your sincere advisor
phrases.explanation: He assured his people that he was transmitting his Lord’s messages to them faithfully and was a trustworthy, sincere adviser in calling them to worship Allah alone without idols, neither lying about Allah’s revelation nor adding to or altering anything of the message entrusted to him.

phrases.translation: Do you find it astonishing that a reminder should come to you from your Lord through one of your own so he may warn you?
phrases.explanation: Hud asked his people why they marvelled that Allah had sent down His revelation and admonition through a man from among their own tribe whom they knew well, in order to warn them of Allah’s might and punishment. Familiarity with the messenger’s upright character should have encouraged belief rather than disdainful surprise.

phrases.translation: Remember that He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you greatly in stature.
phrases.explanation: He urged them to remember how Allah had made them successors inhabiting the earth after destroying Noah’s people for their disobedience, and had favoured them with extraordinary bodily height, size, and physical strength surpassing previous peoples. Their strength and prosperity were gifts from Allah, not guarantees of immunity from His judgment.

phrases.translation: So remember Allah’s favours, so you may be successful.”
phrases.explanation: Hud called upon them to remember Allah’s abundant blessings with grateful obedience by worshipping Him alone and forsaking idols and partners, so that they might attain true success and eternal bliss in the hereafter. Remembering divine favour means using Allah’s gifts in obedience rather than arrogant self-sufficiency.

phrases.translation: They said, “Have you come to us so that we would worship Allah alone and abandon what our forefathers used to worship?
phrases.explanation: Clinging stubbornly to their ancestral idolatry, the people of Ad asked Hud in outrage whether he had come to make them worship Allah alone and forsake the idols and false gods that their forefathers had worshipped before them. Blind loyalty to ancestral custom was their sole argument against the call to pure monotheism.

phrases.translation: Then bring us what you threaten us with, if what you say is true!”
phrases.explanation: Refusing to follow his call to monotheism, they defiantly challenged Hud to bring down upon them at once the divine torment and punishment he had threatened them with, if he was truly a prophet sent from Allah. Demanding immediate punishment was a sign of hardened hearts that mistook divine forbearance for weakness.

phrases.translation: He said, “You will certainly be subjected to your Lord’s torment and wrath.
phrases.explanation: When they demanded the punishment in open defiance, Hud declared that torment, defilement, and inescapable wrath from their Lord had already become due and decreed upon them because of their stubborn rebellion. Once a community demands the very torment it was warned against, its doom is sealed.

phrases.translation: Do you dispute with me regarding the so-called gods which you and your forefathers have made up—a practice Allah has never authorized?
phrases.explanation: He rebuked them for arguing with him in defence of mere empty names of gods that they and their forefathers had invented for lifeless idols of stone and wood that neither harm nor benefit, without any proof or authority ever sent down by Allah. Inventing sacred titles for carved objects cannot give those objects any real divine authority.

phrases.translation: Then wait! I too am waiting with you.”
phrases.explanation: Since they had asked to hasten the torment, Hud told them to wait for the descent of Allah’s inescapable punishment upon them while he waited alongside them for Allah’s decisive judgment between them. Calm confidence in Allah’s promise allowed Hud to face an entire hostile nation without fear.

phrases.translation: So We saved him and those with him by Our mercy
phrases.explanation: When the barren, destructive wind arrived to execute Allah’s decree against the tribe of Ad, Allah saved Hud and the believers who followed him in pure monotheism and affirmed his message by His special mercy and grace. Divine mercy shielded the faithful amidst a catastrophe that swept away the surrounding land.

phrases.translation: and uprooted those who denied Our signs. They were not believers
phrases.explanation: At the same time Allah utterly eradicated those of Hud’s people who denied His proofs down to the very last remnant, leaving none of them alive because they refused to believe in Allah and His messenger. All their physical might and lofty buildings could not preserve a single disbeliever from ruin.

phrases.translation: And to the people of Thamûd We sent their brother Ṣâliḥ. He said, “O my people! Worship Allah—you have no other god except Him.
phrases.explanation: To the tribe of Thamud dwelling in al-Hijr between the Hijaz and Syria, Allah sent their kinsman Salih, who called them to worship Allah alone without partner, declaring that they had no other god worthy of worship beside Him. Like Noah and Hud before him, Salih began by calling his people back to exclusive monotheism.

phrases.translation: A clear proof has come to you from your Lord: this is Allah’s she-camel as a sign to you.
phrases.explanation: Salih announced that a clear proof had come to them from their Lord to confirm his prophethood: the miraculous she-camel that Allah brought forth out of solid rock in answer to their own demand for a sign. Because the miracle answered their own challenge, it left no honest room for doubt.

phrases.translation: So leave her to graze ˹freely˺ on Allah’s land and do not harm her, or else you will be overcome by a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: Salih warned his people to let the miraculous she-camel graze freely on Allah’s earth without hindrance or harm and never touch her with evil or slaughter her, lest a painful punishment from Allah seize them in retribution for defying their Lord’s command. Respecting the sign Allah placed among them was the test of whether they would obey.

phrases.translation: Remember when He made you successors after ’Âd and established you in the land—˹and˺ you built palaces on its plains and carved homes into mountains.
phrases.explanation: Salih reminded Thamud of Allah’s favour when He made them successors in the land after destroying Ad and settled them with such mastery that they built grand palaces on its flat plains and hewed secure dwellings out of its rocky mountains. Their architectural mastery over plains and mountains was a blessing meant to inspire gratitude.

phrases.translation: So remember Allah’s favours, and do not go about spreading corruption in the land.”
phrases.explanation: He urged them to remember the bounties of Allah with gratitude and obedience to His commands, and forbade them from going about the earth working corruption through idolatry and defiance of their Lord. Using divine favours to fuel tyranny and rebellion turns prosperity into a cause of destruction.

phrases.translation: The arrogant chiefs of his people asked the lowly who believed among them, “Are you certain that Ṣâliḥ has been sent by his Lord?”
phrases.explanation: The proud notables of Thamud who disdained following Salih mocked the humble, socially weak believers among his followers by asking whether they truly knew for certain that Salih had been sent as a messenger by his Lord. Arrogant leaders often assume that truth would never be embraced first by the poor and humble.

phrases.translation: They replied, “We certainly believe in what he has been sent with.”
phrases.explanation: Unshaken by the chiefs’ scorn, the humble believers firmly replied that they believed in and affirmed the truth, guidance, and pure monotheism with which Allah had sent His messenger Salih to them. Simple, unwavering certainty in revelation stood firm against the intimidation of the ruling elite.

phrases.translation: The arrogant said, “We surely reject what you believe in.”
phrases.explanation: Swollen with pride against Allah’s command and His messenger Salih, the arrogant chiefs and notables of Thamud declared to the humble believers that they utterly rejected, denied, and disbelieved in the message of prophethood, divine truth, and pure monotheism that the believers had affirmed and embraced.

phrases.translation: Then they killed the she-camel—defying their Lord’s command—
phrases.explanation: In insolent rebellion and haughty defiance against their Lord’s command, Thamud hamstrung and slaughtered the miraculous she-camel that Allah had made a clear sign for them, exalting themselves in falsehood above the truth. Although one man struck the blow, the whole community shared the guilt by approving the crime.

phrases.translation: and challenged ˹Ṣâliḥ˺, “Bring us what you threaten us with, if you are ˹truly˺ one of the messengers.”
phrases.explanation: After slaying the she-camel, they defiantly challenged Salih to hasten and bring down upon them at once the divine punishment and vengeance he had threatened them with, if he was truly one of Allah’s sent messengers. Instead of repenting after their crime, they compounded it by mocking the promised punishment.

phrases.translation: Then an ˹overwhelming˺ earthquake struck them, and they fell lifeless in their homes
phrases.explanation: After the three days’ warning expired, a convulsing shock and terrifying blast from heaven seized those of Thamud who had killed the she-camel, leaving them fallen face down on their knees, lifeless and motionless without a single soul remaining alive across their dwellings and land.

phrases.translation: So he turned away from them, saying, “O my people! Surely I conveyed to you my Lord’s message and gave you ˹sincere˺ advice,
phrases.explanation: Departing from their land as their destruction befell them, Salih addressed his ruined people, declaring that he had faithfully conveyed to them his Lord’s message of command and prohibition and had given them sincere counsel to save them from Allah’s wrath. A prophet is responsible for clear delivery and sincere counsel, not for forcing hearts to believe.

phrases.translation: but you do not like ˹sincere˺ advisors.”
phrases.explanation: Yet they had brought ruin upon themselves because they hated sincere advisers who counselled them for Allah’s sake and called them to abandon their idolatrous desires, arrogance, and lusts in favour of obedience to their Creator. When a community hates those who advise it honestly, it cuts itself off from reform.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when Lot scolded ˹the men of˺ his people,
phrases.explanation: Allah next recalls sending Lot to his people in the cities of Sodom, reminding the Prophet of when Lot rebuked the men of his city for their wicked conduct and warned them against Allah’s wrath and punishment. Prophetic guidance confronts moral corruption directly even when an entire city has normalized the sin.

phrases.translation: ˹saying,˺ “Do you commit a shameful deed that no man has ever done before
phrases.explanation: Lot condemned them for committing a shameful, abominable act of indecency in approaching males sexually, a vile practice that no human community anywhere among the worlds had ever committed before the people of Lot. Their innovation in shamelessness violated both divine command and the natural order created by Allah.

phrases.translation: You lust after men instead of women!
phrases.explanation: Clarifying the abomination for which he rebuked them, Lot condemned his people for approaching men in their hindparts out of lustful desire instead of approaching the women whom Allah had created and made lawful for marriage. Turning away from lawful marriage toward forbidden lust was a deliberate inversion of Allah’s design.

phrases.translation: You are certainly transgressors.”
phrases.explanation: Lot declared that by abandoning what Allah had permitted for them and indulging in what He had strictly forbidden, they were a people who transgressed all bounds in insolent disobedience and rebellion against their Lord. Persisting in what crosses every moral limit marks a people out as wilful transgressors.

phrases.translation: But his people’s only response was to say, “Expel them from your land!
phrases.explanation: When Lot reproached them for their shameful conduct, his people offered no reasoned argument or excuse, but only urged one another in defiance to drive Lot, his family, and his believing followers out of their city. When corrupt societies cannot defend their actions with reason, they resort to silencing the righteous.

phrases.translation: They are a people who wish to remain chaste!”
phrases.explanation: In perverse mockery, the people of Sodom gave as their sole reason for banishing Lot and his followers from their land that they were people who kept themselves pure and aloof from their filthy, forbidden practices. Treating moral purity as a crime reveals how completely their standards had been inverted.

phrases.translation: So We saved him and his family
phrases.explanation: When Lot’s people refused to repent and persisted in their abomination despite his warnings, Allah saved Lot and the believing members of his household by leading them safely out of the doomed city before dawn. Allah rescues those who remain pure for His sake even from the midst of general ruin.

phrases.translation: except his wife, who was one of the doomed
phrases.explanation: Only Lot’s aged, unfaithful wife was excluded from deliverance, for she disbelieved in Allah and betrayed Lot to the wicked townspeople, remaining behind among those doomed to perish in the city’s destruction. Close kinship to a prophet cannot save a person who chooses solidarity with the wicked.

phrases.translation: We poured upon them a rain ˹of brimstone˺.
phrases.explanation: Once Lot and his believing family had departed at Allah’s command, Allah rained down upon the disbelieving people of Sodom a devastating shower of stones of baked clay from heaven that utterly destroyed their towns. The punishment rained down from above turned their prosperous cities into a permanent warning.

phrases.translation: See what was the end of the wicked
phrases.explanation: Allah commands the Prophet to behold the ruinous end of those wicked criminals who defied Allah and His messenger, as a stern warning to the polytheists of Quraysh lest a similar punishment overtake them. History’s ruined settlements testify that defiance of Allah’s messengers always ends in disaster.

phrases.translation: And to the people of Midian We sent their brother Shu’aib. He said, “O my people! Worship Allah—you have no other god except Him. A clear proof has already come to you from your Lord.
phrases.explanation: To the tribe of Midian, descendants of Midian son of Abraham, Allah sent their kinsman Shuaib, who called them to worship Allah alone without any idol or partner beside Him after a clear proof and miracle from their Lord had established the truth of his message.

phrases.translation: So give just measure and weight, do not defraud people of their property,
phrases.explanation: Because the people of Midian coupled idolatry with cheating in commerce, Shuaib commanded them to give full measure and weight in all transactions and never wrong people by diminishing their goods and rightful dues. Pure worship of Allah cannot be separated from honesty and fairness in dealings with people.

phrases.translation: nor spread corruption in the land after it has been set in order. This is for your own good, if you are ˹truly˺ believers
