phrases.explanation: He further forbade them from spreading corruption on earth through disobedience and fraud after Allah had set it in order, assuring them that honesty and obedience to Allah were far better for them if they were true believers. Fair dealing preserves social trust and brings lasting blessing far better than illicit gain.

phrases.translation: And do not lie in ambush on every road—threatening and hindering those who believe in Allah from His Path and striving to make it ˹appear˺ crooked.
phrases.explanation: Shuaib forbade his people from sitting in ambush along every road to intimidate travellers who came seeking him, threatening believers with death, barring people who wished to embrace faith from Allah’s path, and slandering him as a liar to make the true religion appear crooked.

phrases.translation: Remember when you were few, then He increased you in number. And consider the fate of the corruptors
phrases.explanation: He urged them to remember Allah’s favour upon them when they had been few in number and He multiplied them in population, wealth, and strength, and to reflect carefully on the destructive fate that befell earlier nations who spread corruption and disobeyed Allah on earth.

phrases.translation: If some of you do believe in what I have been sent with while others do not, then be patient until Allah judges between us.
phrases.explanation: Shuaib told his people that since one group among them believed in the message of monotheism and fair dealing with which he was sent while another group refused to believe, both sides should wait patiently until Allah delivered His decisive verdict between them. Waiting for Allah’s verdict requires steadfastness from believers and serves as a warning to opponents.

phrases.translation: He is the Best of Judges.”
phrases.explanation: For Allah is the best of all who judge and distinguish between truth and falsehood, and the most just of deciders, in whose judgment there is never any unfairness, inclination, or partiality toward anyone. When Allah judges between a prophet and his deniers, He vindicates the truth beyond dispute.

phrases.translation: The arrogant chiefs of his people threatened, “O Shu’aib! We will certainly expel you and your fellow believers from our land, unless you return to our faith.”
phrases.explanation: The proud notables of Midian who disdained submitting to Allah threatened to banish Shuaib and all who believed with him from their city unless they abandoned Islam and returned to Midian’s idolatrous religion. Threatening exile is the recurring weapon of tyrants who cannot defeat a prophet’s arguments.

phrases.translation: He replied, “Even if we hate it
phrases.explanation: Shuaib answered their ultimatum in astonishment, asking whether they would force him and the believers out of their homeland or compel them to return to a false religion even though they detested its error and knew its falsehood. No true believer can trade the certainty of guidance for a falsehood his heart abhors.

phrases.translation: We would surely be fabricating a lie against Allah if we were to return to your faith after Allah has saved us from it.
phrases.explanation: Shuaib declared that he and the believers would be fabricating a monstrous lie against Allah if they returned to Midian’s false creed after Allah had rescued them from its error and guided them to the truth. Returning to idolatry after knowing the truth would mean slandering Allah with partners He never had.

phrases.translation: It does not befit us to return to it unless it is the Will of Allah, our Lord. Our Lord has encompassed everything in ˹His˺ knowledge.
phrases.explanation: It could never befit them to return to idolatry unless Allah their Lord had so willed in His prior decree, for the knowledge of their Lord encompasses all things that have been and all that will ever be. Believers entrust the preservation of their faith to the all-knowing Lord rather than their own strength.

phrases.translation: In Allah we trust. Our Lord! Judge between us and our people with truth. You are the best of those who judge.”
phrases.explanation: Placing their full reliance upon Allah against their people’s threats of banishment, Shuaib and the believers prayed to their Lord to issue a decisive judgment and separation in truth between them and their disbelieving people, acknowledging Him as the best and most just of all who decide.

phrases.translation: The disbelieving chiefs of his people threatened, “If you follow Shu’aib, you will surely be losers!”
phrases.explanation: Turning to their own townspeople to deter them from faith, the disbelieving leaders of Midian warned one another that if they followed Shuaib in worshipping Allah alone and abandoning their ancestral idolatry and commercial fraud, they would surely suffer ruin in their affairs and become losers.

phrases.translation: Then an ˹overwhelming˺ earthquake struck them and they fell lifeless in their homes
phrases.explanation: In answer to Shuaib’s prayer, Allah’s punishment struck the disbelievers of Midian with a convulsing earthquake and the torment of the scorching canopy of cloud that closed over them, leaving them fallen upon their knees, lifeless and motionless without a single survivor in their dwellings.

phrases.translation: Those who rejected Shu’aib were ˹wiped out˺ as if they had never lived there.
phrases.explanation: Allah utterly uprooted and eradicated those who denied Shuaib, leaving their town empty and desolate at the moment they perished as though they had never resided, settled, or enjoyed prosperity in it before. Generations of wealth and settlement vanished in an instant when Allah’s decree overtook them.

phrases.translation: Those who rejected Shu’aib were the true losers
phrases.explanation: Refuting the disbelieving chiefs’ boast that following Shuaib would bring loss, Allah declares that it was not Shuaib’s followers who lost, but rather those who rejected Shuaib who were the true losers in both worlds. True loss lies not in sacrificing illicit profits for faith, but in losing one’s soul.

phrases.translation: He turned away from them, saying, “O my people! Indeed, I have delivered to you the messages of my Lord and gave you ˹sincere˺ advice.
phrases.explanation: Departing from their midst as Allah’s vengeance descended upon them, Shuaib addressed his ruined people, declaring that he had faithfully delivered to them the messages of his Lord and counselled them sincerely to obey Allah and abandon injustice. Having fulfilled every duty of warning and counsel, Shuaib bore no blame for their ruin.

phrases.translation: How can I then grieve for those who chose to disbelieve?”
phrases.explanation: Consoling himself over the destruction that struck his people, Shuaib asked how he could possibly grieve or feel sorrow over the ruin of a people who stubbornly denied Allah’s oneness and rejected His messenger. Those who deliberately reject every offer of mercy leave no ground for regret when judgment falls.

phrases.translation: Whenever We sent a prophet to a society, We afflicted its ˹disbelieving˺ people with suffering and adversity,
phrases.explanation: Describing His established way with bygone nations to warn Quraysh, Allah states that whenever He sent a prophet to a town and its inhabitants denied him, He seized them with extreme poverty, hunger, and bodily affliction. Hardship is sent first as a wake-up call to break human arrogance before final destruction.

phrases.translation: so perhaps they would be humbled
phrases.explanation: Allah sent those hardships and trials upon them as a merciful warning so that their pride might be broken and they might humble themselves in sincere submission, repentance, and obedience before their Lord. Tribulation achieves its merciful purpose only when it drives people back to humble supplication.

phrases.translation: Then We changed their adversity to prosperity until they flourished and argued ˹falsely˺, “Our forefathers ˹too˺ had been visited by adversity and prosperity.”
phrases.explanation: When hardship did not humble them, Allah replaced their distress with health, wealth, and abundant offspring as a test, yet instead of giving thanks they multiplied and dismissed their earlier trials as ordinary ups and downs of time like those their forefathers experienced. By treating both trial and relief as mere chance, they blinded themselves to Allah’s warning.

phrases.translation: So We seized them by surprise, while they were unaware
phrases.explanation: Because they failed to recognize Allah’s test or repent during their ease and prosperity, Allah seized them suddenly with utter destruction at a moment when they felt secure and did not perceive punishment approaching. Prosperity without gratitude becomes a snare that lulls the heedless until judgment strikes.

phrases.translation: Had the people of those societies been faithful and mindful ˹of Allah˺, We would have overwhelmed them with blessings from heaven and earth.
phrases.explanation: Had the inhabitants of those destroyed towns believed in Allah and His messengers and been mindful of Him by obeying His commands and shunning idolatry, Allah would have opened upon them abundant blessings of rain from heaven and fertile vegetation from the earth. Faith and mindfulness of Allah bring harmony between human society and the blessings of creation.

phrases.translation: But they disbelieved, so We seized them for what they used to commit
phrases.explanation: Instead of believing and fearing Allah, they stubbornly denied His messengers and rejected His signs, so Allah seized them with devastating punishment in just requital for the evil deeds and sins they used to earn. Destruction was not an arbitrary misfortune, but the direct fruit of their own persistent deeds.

phrases.translation: Did the people of those societies feel secure that Our punishment would not come upon them by night while they were asleep
phrases.explanation: Warning the disbelieving townspeople who persist in idolatry and denial, Allah asks whether they feel safe and secure from His overwhelming punishment and vengeance descending upon them suddenly at night while they lie asleep and heedless in their beds, just as ruin overtook earlier rebellious communities.

phrases.translation: Or did they feel secure that Our punishment would not come upon them by day while they were at play
phrases.explanation: Or do the inhabitants of those disbelieving towns feel safe and secure that Allah’s mighty punishment and vengeance will not strike them suddenly in the bright forenoon while they are heedlessly absorbed in worldly amusement and idle play, just as swift destruction overtook past rebellious nations?.

phrases.translation: Did they feel secure against Allah’s planning?
phrases.explanation: Allah asks whether those who deny His signs and messengers feel secure from His subtle plan, whereby He grants disbelievers health, wealth, and worldly ease that gradually draw them on to destruction while they persist in sin. Worldly respite granted to unrepentant sinners is a test, not a sign of divine approval.

phrases.translation: None would feel secure from Allah’s planning except the losers
phrases.explanation: No one feels safe from Allah’s gradual drawing of sinners to ruin while continuing to disobey Him and reject His clear signs except a people who are utterly doomed to loss and destruction in both worlds. Feeling safe from accountability while persisting in rebellion is the hallmark of spiritual ruin.

phrases.translation: Is it not clear to those who take over the land after ˹the destruction of˺ its former residents that—if We will—We can punish them ˹too˺ for their sins
phrases.explanation: Has it not become clear to those who inherit the earth as successors after the destruction of its former inhabitants, yet still imitate their disobedience, that if Allah willed He could strike them down for their sins just as He destroyed those before them? Inheriting the lands of vanished nations should awaken reverent caution rather than repeat their sins.

phrases.translation: and seal their hearts so they will not hear ˹the truth˺
phrases.explanation: And has it not become clear to them that Allah can seal up their hearts because of their rebellion so that they cannot hear any admonition or reminder with a hearing that benefits them or leads them to repent? When a heart is sealed through persistent defiance, even the clearest warnings no longer penetrate.

phrases.translation: We have narrated to you ˹O Prophet˺ some of the stories of those societies. Surely, their messengers came to them with clear proofs,
phrases.explanation: Addressing the Prophet after recounting the histories of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shuaib, Allah states that He has related the news of those destroyed towns whose messengers came to them with unmistakable miracles and proofs establishing the truth of their prophethood. These historical accounts remind the Prophet and his community that opposition to clear revelation is an ancient pattern.

phrases.translation: but still they would not believe in what they had already denied.
phrases.explanation: Yet those peoples would not believe when their messengers arrived in what they had already denied before, whether because of their prior denial since the covenant taken from them in Adam’s loins or according to Allah’s prior knowledge and decree. Once a community hardens itself in stubborn denial, even the arrival of open miracles fails to move it to faith.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah seals the hearts of the disbelievers
phrases.explanation: Just as Allah sealed the hearts of those destroyed nations so they refused to believe the clear proofs of their messengers, so too does Allah set a seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers among the Prophet’s own people who reject his call. Persistent rejection of truth eventually deprives the heart of the capacity to benefit from further reminders.

phrases.translation: We did not find most of them true to their covenant.
phrases.explanation: Allah states that He did not find most of those bygone nations faithful to the primordial covenant taken from them when they were brought forth from Adam’s loins to acknowledge that Allah alone is their Lord. Instead of honouring that pledge when messengers reminded them of it, they broke their word and worshipped false deities.

phrases.translation: Rather, We found most of them truly rebellious
phrases.explanation: Far from keeping their covenant with Allah, most of the inhabitants of those societies proved to be defiant rebels who stepped outside obedience to their Lord and violated His commands. Their history demonstrates that majority practice in a corrupt society is no measure of fidelity to Allah.

phrases.translation: Then after them We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they wrongfully rejected them.
phrases.explanation: After the messengers of those earlier nations, Allah sent Moses with clear signs and miracles to Pharaoh, the tyrannical ruler of Egypt, and the leading nobles of his Coptic people, yet they wrongfully denied and disbelieved in those signs out of sheer injustice and arrogance. They rejected the truth not for lack of evidence, but to preserve their worldly dominance.

phrases.translation: See what was the end of the corruptors
phrases.explanation: Allah commands the Prophet to behold the final outcome of those who spread corruption on earth by disobeying Allah and denying His messenger, when Allah drowned them in the sea before the eyes of the Children of Israel. Their ruin stands as a warning to every tyrant who fights against divine revelation.

phrases.translation: And Moses said, “O Pharaoh! I am truly a messenger from the Lord of all worlds
phrases.explanation: Standing before the tyrant of Egypt, Moses proclaimed directly to Pharaoh that he was a true messenger sent by the Sovereign Creator and Lord of all worlds, thereby refuting Pharaoh’s pretension to lordship and summoning him to submit to the One who rules all creation.

phrases.translation: obliged to say nothing about Allah except the truth.
phrases.explanation: Moses declared that it was incumbent and binding upon him, or according to another reading that he was duty-bound and worthy, to speak nothing concerning Allah except the pure truth without fabrication or falsehood. A true prophet speaks only what Allah has revealed and authorised.

phrases.translation: Indeed, I have come to you with clear proof from your Lord, so let the children of Israel go with me.”
phrases.explanation: Moses announced that he had brought Pharaoh an unmistakable miracle from his Lord proving the truth of his mission, and demanded that Pharaoh release the enslaved Children of Israel from bondage and allow them to go free with him to worship Allah. Liberation of the oppressed stood at the heart of his prophetic summons.

phrases.translation: Pharaoh said, “If you have come with a sign, then bring it
phrases.explanation: Challenging Moses’ claim before the royal court, Pharaoh demanded that if Moses had indeed brought a miraculous sign from the Lord who sent him, he should produce and display it before him at once. Pharaoh hoped to expose Moses as an impostor in front of his nobles.

phrases.translation: if what you say is true.”
phrases.explanation: Pharaoh added that producing such a sign was required to prove that Moses was telling the truth in claiming to be a messenger from the Lord of all worlds obliged to speak only truth about Allah. By setting this public condition, Pharaoh left himself no excuse once the miracle appeared.

phrases.translation: So Moses threw down his staff and—behold!—it became a real snake
phrases.explanation: Answering Pharaoh’s challenge immediately, Moses cast the wooden staff from his hand onto the ground, and before the eyes of all present it transformed into a huge, manifest serpent, an unmistakable living python rather than a mere trick of the eye or illusion. By turning dry wood into a living creature, Allah showed a sign that no human craft could imitate.

phrases.translation: Then he drew his hand ˹out of his collar˺
phrases.explanation: Displaying a second miraculous proof right after the serpent, Moses placed his hand inside the bosom of his garment and drew it forth before Pharaoh and his assembly. This second sign complemented the staff by showing divine power within Moses’ own body. Together the two miracles demonstrated that the Creator governs both inanimate objects and living bodies.

phrases.translation: and it was ˹shining˺ white for all to see
phrases.explanation: Although Moses was dark-complexioned in skin, his hand emerged shining with a brilliant, radiant whiteness like light, completely free of leprosy or disease, as a clear miracle for all onlookers to behold. Once he returned his hand to his garment, it reverted to its normal colour.

phrases.translation: The chiefs of Pharaoh’s people said, “He is indeed a skilled magician
phrases.explanation: Stunned by the staff becoming a serpent and the radiant white hand yet unwilling to submit to Allah’s truth, the leading nobles of Pharaoh’s people dismissed the miracles by claiming that Moses was merely a learned, accomplished sorcerer who bewitched people’s eyes. Branding a prophet a magician was their way of acknowledging the wonder while denying its divine origin.

phrases.translation: who seeks to drive you from your land.”
phrases.explanation: To stir up fear and hostility against Moses, the chiefs claimed that through his signs Moses sought to expel Pharaoh and the Copts from their homeland of Egypt and seize royal power for the Children of Israel. Tyrants routinely portray a call to truth as a political plot against the nation.

phrases.translation: ˹So Pharaoh asked,˺ “What do you propose?”
phrases.explanation: Alarmed for his throne and consulting his inner circle, Pharaoh asked his chiefs what course of action they advised him to take regarding Moses and the signs he had displayed. For all his boasts of absolute power, Pharaoh stood baffled and dependent on his advisers.

phrases.translation: They replied, “Let him and his brother wait
phrases.explanation: Pharaoh’s chiefs advised him to put off Moses and his brother Aaron for a time without rushing to execute them, delaying the confrontation until preparations could be made across the kingdom. They feared that hasty violence might only strengthen Moses’ appeal among the people. Buying time allowed the regime to rally its resources instead of conceding defeat in the royal court.

phrases.translation: and send mobilizers to all cities
phrases.explanation: Meanwhile, they counselled Pharaoh to dispatch heralds, musterers, and guards throughout all the cities and provinces of Egypt to gather the most capable practitioners of magic in the realm. They assumed that state power and numbers could overwhelm the sign Moses had brought. By turning the contest into a public spectacle, Pharaoh inadvertently gathered witnesses for the triumph of truth.

phrases.translation: to bring you every clever magician.”
phrases.explanation: The purpose of sending musterers across Egypt’s cities was to assemble before Pharaoh every skilled, deeply learned sorcerer who excelled in the craft of magic, so that they could match Moses’ signs with their own illusions and defeat him in public view. They trusted that the finest specialists in Egypt would expose or outdo whatever Moses had brought.

phrases.translation: The magicians came to Pharaoh,
phrases.explanation: When the master sorcerers gathered from across the cities of Egypt and arrived at Pharaoh’s court for the appointed contest with Moses, they approached the king as mercenaries seeking worldly advancement. Their initial concern was royal patronage rather than religious truth. Their opening question shows they entered the field for royal pay and status rather than conviction.

phrases.translation: saying, “Shall we receive a ˹suitable˺ reward if we prevail?”
phrases.explanation: Before entering the contest, the magicians bargained with Pharaoh, asking whether they would be guaranteed a generous payment and reward from him if they overcame Moses and defeated his signs. Falsehood relies on material incentives to rally its champions. Unlike prophets who ask no wage from people, the sorcerers demanded assurance of payment in advance.

phrases.translation: He replied, “Yes,
phrases.explanation: Eager to secure their utmost effort against Moses, Pharaoh immediately promised the magicians that they would indeed receive the generous material reward and wealth they had requested if they prevailed. He spared no promise to protect his rule. Worldly rulers readily promise wealth and privilege when their authority feels threatened by the truth.

phrases.translation: and you will certainly be among those closest to me.”
phrases.explanation: Beyond mere payment, Pharaoh promised that if they defeated Moses they would be elevated into his inner circle of honoured courtiers and trusted companions nearest to the throne. Ironically, within moments those very magicians would spurn Pharaoh’s court for closeness to Allah. Royal nearness was the highest prize Pharaoh could offer, yet faith would soon make it worthless to them.

phrases.translation: They asked, “O Moses! Will you cast,
phrases.explanation: Standing arrayed on the field of contest before the assembled crowds, the magicians addressed Moses with formal courtesy, asking whether he wished to cast down his staff first. Even before believing, their respectful manner prepared the way for their recognition of the truth. Their polite challenge before the crowd heightened the suspense of the confrontation.

phrases.translation: or shall we be the first to cast?”
phrases.explanation: Or, they asked, should they be the ones to throw down their ropes and staffs before he cast his. By offering Moses the choice, they set the stage for their own illusions to be displayed at full strength before Allah’s sign obliterated them. Allowing them to choose or go first removed any claim that Moses had caught them unprepared.

phrases.translation: Moses said, “You first.”
phrases.explanation: Confident in Allah’s support, Moses told the magicians to cast their ropes and staffs first so that the people could witness the full extent of their sorcery before truth swept it away. Letting falsehood spend its force first made the triumph of the miracle unmistakable.

phrases.translation: So when they did, they deceived the eyes of the people, stunned them, and made a great display of magic
phrases.explanation: When the magicians threw down their thick ropes and wooden staffs, they bewitched the eyes of the spectators so the objects appeared to writhe like snakes, striking terror into the onlookers and producing a mighty display of illusion without changing the actual nature of the ropes and wood.

phrases.translation: Then We inspired Moses, “Throw down your staff,”
phrases.explanation: At the height of the magicians’ illusion, Allah revealed to Moses the command to cast down the staff in his right hand without fear or hesitation. Divine revelation intervened at the decisive moment to distinguish prophetic miracle from human trickery. Calm obedience to Allah’s command sufficed to overturn the most elaborate spectacle of falsehood.

phrases.translation: and—behold!—it devoured the objects of their illusion
phrases.explanation: Instantly the staff became a massive serpent that went about swallowing up one after another all the ropes and wooden rods with which the magicians had faked snakes to deceive people’s eyes. When Moses picked it up again, it returned to a simple staff with every false object gone.

phrases.translation: So the truth prevailed and their illusions failed
phrases.explanation: Through that public miracle the truth brought by Moses from Allah was established and made manifest before all onlookers, while every illusion and sorcerous trick that Pharaoh’s magicians had wrought proved utterly vain and vanished without a trace. What rests on divine reality endures, while what rests on deception collapses as soon as truth appears.

phrases.translation: So Pharaoh and his people were defeated right there
phrases.explanation: Right there on the very field of assembly they had organised to humiliate Moses, Pharaoh and his nobles suffered a decisive, undeniable defeat before the eyes of the entire nation. The spectacle intended to crush the truth became the arena of its victory. The very assembly Pharaoh convened to vindicate his rule witnessed the collapse of his case.

phrases.translation: and put to shame
phrases.explanation: Instead of winning glory, Pharaoh and his faction turned back disgraced, humiliated, and empty-handed as their champion magicians abandoned their cause and embraced Moses’ faith on the spot. Public arrogance against Allah’s signs ended in public ignominy. Those who sought to humiliate Allah’s messenger left the field bearing the humiliation themselves.

phrases.translation: And the magicians fell down, prostrating
phrases.explanation: Knowing the limits of magic better than anyone else and realizing with certainty that Moses’ staff was a true miracle from Almighty Allah rather than human sorcery, all the magicians immediately threw themselves down upon their faces in humble prostration to Allah. Because they understood the craft of illusion from the inside, they recognized a genuine miracle immediately.

phrases.translation: They declared, “We ˹now˺ believe in the Lord of all worlds—
phrases.explanation: Openly renouncing Pharaoh’s claim to divinity before the assembled crowds, the prostrating magicians proclaimed that they believed in and submitted to the Sovereign Creator and Lord of all worlds, whose power had just vanquished their illusions. In a single moment the hired defenders of falsehood became fearless witnesses to monotheism.

phrases.translation: the Lord of Moses and Aaron.”
phrases.explanation: To leave no room for Pharaoh to pretend that they meant him by the Lord of all worlds, the magicians explicitly specified that they believed in the Lord of Moses and Aaron, who had sent both brothers with unmistakable truth. Their explicit clarification blocked Pharaoh from claiming that their prostration and confession were meant for him.

phrases.translation: Pharaoh threatened, “How dare you believe in him before I give you permission?
phrases.explanation: Furious that his own champions had publicly embraced faith, Pharaoh rebuked the magicians for daring to believe in Moses and affirm his truthfulness without first obtaining royal permission from him. In his tyranny, Pharaoh imagined that even human conscience required his licence. Arrogant rulers cannot bear to see hearts submit to truth without asking leave of the state.

phrases.translation: This must be a conspiracy you devised in the city to drive out its people, but soon you will see
phrases.explanation: To cover his humiliation before the public, Pharaoh falsely accused the magicians and Moses of having plotted a secret conspiracy in the capital city of Egypt to expel its Coptic inhabitants, and threatened that they would soon learn the terrible consequences of their act. Inventing a conspiracy theory was Pharaoh’s desperate attempt to explain away his own experts’ conversion.

phrases.translation: I will certainly cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides,
phrases.explanation: Unleashing his rage, Pharaoh swore that he would mutilate every one of the believing magicians by cutting off their right hands and left feet on alternate sides as an exemplary punishment. When arguments fail, tyranny falls back on sheer bodily cruelty. Extreme brutality was meant to terrify the public and punish the magicians for defying royal authority.

phrases.translation: then crucify you all.”
phrases.explanation: After amputating their limbs on opposite sides, Pharaoh vowed to crucify them all together upon the trunks of palm trees along the banks of the Nile to terrorize anyone else who might follow Moses. Yet his horrific threat could not shake hearts newly illuminated by faith.

phrases.translation: They responded, “Surely to our Lord we will ˹all˺ return
phrases.explanation: Unmoved by Pharaoh’s threats of mutilation and crucifixion, the believing magicians answered calmly that whatever he did to their bodies in this fleeting world would only hasten their return to their Lord in the hereafter, where everlasting reward awaited them. Certainty in the hereafter freed them from the fear through which Pharaoh controlled his subjects.

phrases.translation: Your rage towards us is only because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us.
phrases.explanation: The magicians told Pharaoh that he held no fault or grudge against them other than that they had believed in the clear signs and proofs of their Lord as soon as those signs appeared before them. Being punished solely for embracing truth was an honour rather than a disgrace.

phrases.translation: Our Lord! Shower us with perseverance, and let us die while submitting ˹to You˺.”
phrases.explanation: Turning from Pharaoh to Allah in prayer, they beseeched their Lord to pour down abundant patience and steadfastness upon them during torture so they would not relapse into disbelief, and to take their souls while they remained steadfast Muslims submitting wholly to Him. Their final supplication asked not for worldly rescue, but for steadfastness until they met Allah as believers.

phrases.translation: The chiefs of Pharaoh’s people protested, “Are you going to leave Moses and his people free to spread corruption in the land and abandon you and your gods?”
phrases.explanation: Inciting Pharaoh after his defeat by Moses, the Coptic nobles asked whether he would leave Moses and the Children of Israel free to spread corruption in Egypt by calling people to disobey Pharaoh and to abandon worshipping him and the idols he had set up for them.

phrases.translation: He responded, “We will kill their sons and keep their women. We will completely dominate them.”
phrases.explanation: Pharaoh answered that he would renew the slaughter of the newborn sons of the Children of Israel while sparing their daughters for service, boasting that his regime held absolute, irresistible dominance and power over them. He did not realize that his tyranny was hastening his own doom.

phrases.translation: Moses reassured his people, “Seek Allah’s help and be patient.
phrases.explanation: Hearing Pharaoh’s renewed threat to slaughter their sons, Moses comforted the frightened Children of Israel by commanding them to seek help from Allah alone against their oppressor and to endure their trial with steadfast patience. Reliance upon Allah and patient perseverance are the twin weapons of believers facing tyranny.

phrases.translation: Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah ˹alone˺. He grants it to whoever He chooses of His servants. The ultimate outcome belongs ˹only˺ to the righteous.”
phrases.explanation: Moses reminded them that the entire earth belongs to Allah rather than Pharaoh, that Allah bequeaths it as an inheritance to whomever He wills among His servants, and that the blessed final outcome of victory and Paradise belongs to those who fear Allah and obey Him.

phrases.translation: They complained, “We have always been oppressed—before and after you came to us ˹with the message˺.”
phrases.explanation: Distressed by the long years of persecution, the Children of Israel complained to Moses that Pharaoh had tormented them by slaughtering their sons and enslaving their people both before Moses was sent to them and again after he arrived with his message. Long-drawn hardship tested their faith before the promised deliverance arrived.

phrases.translation: He replied, “Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land to see what you will do.”
phrases.explanation: Moses gave them the glad promise that their Lord would soon destroy their enemy Pharaoh, make them successors ruling the land after his fall, and then test them by observing whether they would act with gratitude and obedience or fall into wrongdoing. Deliverance from oppression is itself a moral test of how the rescued community will govern.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We afflicted Pharaoh’s people with famine and shortage of crops
phrases.explanation: In response to Pharaoh’s tyranny and refusal to release the Children of Israel, Allah seized Pharaoh’s people with years of severe drought, barrenness, and a drastic loss of crops and fruits from their estates and palm groves. Economic and agricultural blows struck at the pride of a regime that boasted of Egypt’s rivers and wealth.

phrases.translation: so they might come back ˹to their senses˺
phrases.explanation: Allah sent those years of famine and agricultural loss as a warning trial so that Pharaoh’s people might take heed, recognize their helplessness before the Creator, repent of their arrogance, and stop opposing Allah’s messenger. Worldly afflictions are mercifully sent to awaken reflection before irreversible punishment descends.

phrases.translation: In times of prosperity, they said, “This is what we deserve,”
phrases.explanation: Whenever fertile harvests, abundance, and health came to Pharaoh’s people, they boasted that such prosperity was theirs by right because they deserved it, refusing to thank Allah or acknowledge His grace upon them. Ingratitude claims every blessing as personal merit while refusing to see the hand of the Giver.

phrases.translation: but in adversity, they blamed it on Moses and those with him.
phrases.explanation: Yet whenever drought, blight, or hardship struck them, they superstitiously blamed their misfortune on the evil omen and bad luck of Moses and the believers with him instead of recognizing the consequence of their own sins. Superstitious scapegoating allowed them to blame the righteous for disasters caused by their own rebellion.

phrases.translation: Surely all is destined by Allah. Yet most of them did not know
phrases.explanation: Refuting their superstition, Allah declares that every decree of prosperity and calamity they experienced came solely from Allah’s ordainment and judgment upon them, though most of Pharaoh’s people were too ignorant to understand that their afflictions resulted from their own disbelief. Both ease and hardship unfold by Allah’s decree as tests of gratitude and repentance.

phrases.translation: They said, “No matter what sign you may bring to deceive us,
phrases.explanation: Hardening their hearts further, Pharaoh’s people told Moses that whatever miracle, proof, or plague he might bring before them in order to bewitch them and turn them away from their ancestral religion, they would dismiss it as sorcery. Calling clear miracles sorcery was their pretext for refusing to examine the truth of Moses’ message.

phrases.translation: we will never believe in you.”
phrases.explanation: They declared outright that they would never believe in him or submit to his message no matter how many signs they witnessed. This brazen confession proved that their rejection stemmed from stubborn defiance rather than any lack of evidence. Such open obstinacy showed that their hearts were locked against faith regardless of the proofs shown.

phrases.translation: So We plagued them with floods, locusts, lice, frogs, and blood—all as clear signs,
phrases.explanation: Because of their stubborn defiance, Allah sent upon Pharaoh’s people five distinct plagues one after another: devastating floods or epidemics, swarms of locusts devouring crops, lice or ticks infesting food and bodies, frogs filling homes and vessels, and water turning into blood for the Copts.

phrases.translation: but they persisted in arrogance and were a wicked people
phrases.explanation: Although these plagues were sent at separate intervals as unmistakable signs for them to repent, Pharaoh’s people haughtily disdained believing in Allah and obeying Moses, proving themselves to be a wicked people steeped in rebellion. Each plague demonstrated Allah’s control over nature, yet pride kept them from humbling themselves.

phrases.translation: When tormented, they pleaded, “O Moses! Pray to your Lord on our behalf, by virtue of the covenant He made with you.
phrases.explanation: Each time one of those devastating plagues descended upon them and they could no longer bear the distress, they rushed to Moses pleading with him to pray to his Lord on their behalf by virtue of the prophetic covenant and honour Allah had granted him.

phrases.translation: If you help remove this torment from us, we will certainly believe in you and let the Children of Israel go with you.”
phrases.explanation: In their desperation they solemnly promised Moses that if Allah lifted the plague from them through his supplication, they would surely believe in his prophethood and release the Children of Israel to go free with him. Their repeated pleas to Moses proved that in moments of crisis they knew only his Lord could save them.

phrases.translation: But as soon as We removed the torment from them—until they met their inevitable fate—
phrases.explanation: Yet whenever Allah answered Moses’ prayer and lifted the plague from them for a fixed term extending until the appointed hour when their final destruction by drowning was decreed to arrive, their fear vanished at once. Divine forbearance granted them relief time after time until their decreed term reached its end.

phrases.translation: they broke their promise
phrases.explanation: The moment relief returned, Pharaoh and his people treacherously broke the solemn covenant they had made with Moses, neither believing in him nor letting the Children of Israel go, and reverted immediately to their tyranny. Breaking solemn promises made under distress revealed the deep hypocrisy of their temporary remorse.

phrases.translation: So We inflicted punishment upon them, drowning them in the sea
phrases.explanation: When the appointed term of their respite expired after repeated broken promises, Allah exacted His just vengeance upon Pharaoh, his armies, and his chiefs by drowning them all together in the surging waters of the sea. The sea that parted as a road of salvation for the believers closed as a grave over the tyrants.

phrases.translation: for denying Our signs and being heedless of them
phrases.explanation: Allah destroyed them in the sea because they persistently denied the nine clear signs shown to them through Moses and remained willfully heedless of the warnings and lessons those miracles carried. Treating repeated divine warnings with deliberate indifference eventually brings an inescapable reckoning from which no worldly power can save.

phrases.translation: And ˹so˺ We made the oppressed people successors of the eastern and western lands, which We had showered with blessings.
phrases.explanation: After drowning Pharaoh, Allah made the Children of Israel, who had been enslaved and oppressed through the slaughter of their sons, inheritors and rulers of the eastern and western parts of the fertile land of Syria and the Levant, which Allah had blessed with flowing rivers, crops, and fruits.

phrases.translation: ˹In this way˺ the noble Word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel for what they had endured.
phrases.explanation: Thus the gracious promise of their Lord spoken through Moses that He would destroy their enemy and make them successors in the land was fulfilled in full for the Children of Israel as a reward for their patient endurance of Pharaoh’s persecution. Patient endurance under trial was rewarded when Allah fulfilled His promise of deliverance and succession.

phrases.translation: And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people constructed and what they established
phrases.explanation: At the same time Allah ruined and laid waste the grand palaces, monuments, and edifices that Pharaoh and his people had constructed across Egypt, along with the trellised vineyards and orchards they had raised up. Every monument of tyranny they built to project permanence was reduced to ruin.

phrases.translation: We brought the Children of Israel across the sea and they came upon a people devoted to idols.
phrases.explanation: After Allah brought the Children of Israel safely across the parted sea and drowned their enemy behind them, they passed by a pagan tribe who were sitting in devotion around idols shaped like cattle that they worshipped beside Allah. Long exposure to Egypt’s pagan culture left some among them vulnerable to the lure of visible idols.

phrases.translation: They demanded, “O Moses! Make for us a god like their gods.” He replied, “Indeed, you are a people acting ignorantly
phrases.explanation: Forgetting the mighty miracles they had just witnessed, some of the Children of Israel asked Moses to fashion for them a visible idol to worship just like those pagans had. Moses rebuked them sharply, declaring that they were a people ignorant of Allah’s greatness and exclusive right to worship.

phrases.translation: What they follow is certainly doomed to destruction
phrases.explanation: Moses explained to his people that the idolatrous religion and false worship in which those pagans were engaged was utterly doomed to ruin, perdition, and divine wrath. What appears impressive to the ignorant eye is in reality a path to destruction. False worship carries no future except ruin for those who cling to it.

phrases.translation: and their deeds are in vain.”
phrases.explanation: Moreover, all the devotion, sacrifices, and rituals that those idolaters performed for their false gods were completely void and worthless, bringing them no reward or benefit whatsoever in this world or the hereafter. No amount of ritual effort can make idol worship acceptable or fruitful before Allah.

phrases.translation: He added, “Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah,
phrases.explanation: In astonished reproach, Moses asked his people how they could expect him to seek for them any deity to worship other than Allah, the true Creator who alone possesses divinity and power. Worshipping anything created is an insult to the Creator who alone possesses lordship.

phrases.translation: while He has honoured you above the others?”
phrases.explanation: How could they ask for an idol when it was Allah alone who had favoured and exalted them above all other peoples of their era by choosing prophets from among them and delivering them from bondage? Special divine favour demands deeper gratitude and purer monotheism rather than imitation of idolaters.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when We rescued you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with dreadful torment—killing your sons and keeping your women.
phrases.explanation: Reminding the Children of Israel of His supreme favour upon their forefathers, Allah recalls how He rescued them from Pharaoh’s followers, who had subjected them to the worst torment by slaughtering their newborn sons and sparing their daughters for humiliating servitude. Recalling the horrors of past bondage should awaken lasting thankfulness to the One who set them free.

phrases.translation: That was a severe test from your Lord
phrases.explanation: Both the terrible persecution they suffered under Pharaoh’s tyranny and the miraculous deliverance by which Allah saved them and drowned their enemies in the sea constituted a tremendous trial and test of gratitude from their Lord. Both the bitter trial of slavery and the grace of rescue tested whether they would remain faithful.

phrases.translation: We appointed for Moses thirty nights then added another ten—completing his Lord’s term of forty nights.
phrases.explanation: Allah appointed thirty nights for Moses to fast and worship in preparation for receiving the Torah, mostly identified with Dhu al-Qadah, and then completed the term with ten more nights of Dhu al-Hijjah so that the appointed communion with his Lord reached forty nights in full.

phrases.translation: Moses commanded his brother Aaron, “Take my place among my people, do what is right, and do not follow the way of the corruptors.”
phrases.explanation: Before departing for the mountain to meet his Lord, Moses placed his brother Aaron in charge of the Children of Israel as his deputy, commanding him to lead them uprightly in obedience to Allah and never follow the path of those who work corruption through sin.

phrases.translation: When Moses came at the appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he asked, “My Lord! Reveal Yourself to me so I may see You.”
phrases.explanation: When Moses arrived at Mount Sinai at the appointed time of forty nights and his Lord spoke to him directly without an intermediary, the sweetness of hearing Allah’s speech filled Moses with longing to behold Him, so he asked his Lord to enable him to see Him.

phrases.translation: Allah answered, “You cannot see Me! But look at the mountain. If it remains firm in its place, only then will you see Me.”
phrases.explanation: Allah replied that Moses could not bear to see Him in this mortal life, and instructed him instead to look toward the mighty mountain, explaining that if the solid rock could remain firm in its place when Allah manifested His glory, then Moses would be able to see Him.

phrases.translation: When his Lord appeared to the mountain, He levelled it to dust and Moses collapsed unconscious.
phrases.explanation: When his Lord manifested a tiny measure of His light and majesty to the mountain, described in early reports as the measure of the tip of a little finger, the entire mountain was pulverized into level dust and Moses fell down unconscious in awe. If solid granite shattered at the manifestation of divine majesty, mortal flesh could never withstand it in this life.

phrases.translation: When he recovered, he cried, “Glory be to You! I turn to You in repentance and I am the first of the believers.”
phrases.explanation: As soon as Moses regained consciousness and realized that no living creature in this world can endure beholding Allah before dying, he exalted Allah’s majesty, repented for having asked to see Him in this life, and declared himself the foremost of the believers among his people.

phrases.translation: Allah said, “O Moses! I have ˹already˺ elevated you above all others by My messages and speech.
phrases.explanation: Consoling and honouring Moses after he was denied vision in this world, Allah told him that He had chosen and exalted him above all the people of his age by entrusting him with His prophetic messages and by speaking to him directly without an intermediary.

phrases.translation: So hold firmly to what I have given you and be grateful.”
phrases.explanation: Allah commanded Moses to receive the Scripture, commandments, and honour granted to him with firm resolve and diligent obedience, and to be among those who show sincere gratitude to Allah for His extraordinary favours. Receiving extraordinary spiritual privilege obliges a servant to hold fast to obedience with gratitude.

phrases.translation: We wrote for him on the Tablets ˹the fundamentals˺ of everything; commandments and explanations of all things.
phrases.explanation: Allah inscribed for Moses upon the Tablets of the Torah comprehensive instruction regarding every religious matter his community needed: admonitions to inspire reverence and detailed explanations of all lawful and unlawful rulings, commands, and prohibitions. The revealed Tablets provided a complete moral and legal foundation for the community’s life.

phrases.translation: ˹We commanded,˺ “Hold to this firmly and ask your people to take the best of it.
phrases.explanation: Allah commanded Moses to hold fast to the Torah with earnest determination and to instruct the Children of Israel to follow its noblest and best teachings, namely its obligations and commands rather than what it prohibited. Taking the best of revelation means embracing its commands whole-heartedly rather than seeking loopholes.

phrases.translation: I will soon show ˹all of˺ you the home of the rebellious
phrases.explanation: Ending with a solemn warning, Allah declared that as they journeyed through the land He would soon show them the ruined dwellings of the defiant nations before them who rebelled against Allah’s commands and perished, or the abode of Hellfire awaiting the rebellious. Seeing the ruined homes of past rebels warns believers against following their path of disobedience.

phrases.translation: I will turn away from My signs those who act unjustly with arrogance in the land.
phrases.explanation: Allah declares that He will turn away from understanding His revelations and pondering the lessons of His signs in creation those who exalt themselves in haughty arrogance upon the earth without right, scorning obedience to Allah and His messengers. Arrogance against truth blinds the heart so that even clear signs no longer yield understanding.

phrases.translation: And even if they were to see every sign, they still would not believe in them. If they see the Right Path, they will not take it. But if they see a crooked path, they will follow it.
phrases.explanation: Blinded by pride, such arrogant people would refuse to believe even if they witnessed every miracle, and whenever they see the straight path of guidance they refuse to follow it, whereas whenever they see a path of error and blindness they eagerly adopt it as their religion.

phrases.translation: This is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them
phrases.explanation: Allah turns their hearts away from guidance into such perversity as a just punishment because they deliberately denied His clear signs and remained heedless of reflecting upon their truth and warning. Spiritual blindness is not an arbitrary fate, but the consequence of scorning Allah’s signs.

phrases.translation: The deeds of those who deny Our signs and the meeting ˹with Allah˺ in the Hereafter will be in vain.
phrases.explanation: Those who reject Allah’s revelations and messengers and deny that they will be resurrected to meet their Lord in the hereafter will find all their worldly deeds nullified and void of any reward on the Day of Judgment. Without faith in Allah’s signs and the hereafter, outward actions have no lasting weight on Judgment Day.

phrases.translation: Will they be rewarded except for what they have done?”
phrases.explanation: In the hereafter they will be recompensed strictly according to the disbelief and disobedience they committed in the world, proving that Allah never wrongs anyone when He requites evil with its like. Divine justice ensures that every person’s final recompense corresponds to what he actually earned.

phrases.translation: In the absence of Moses, his people made from their ˹golden˺ jewellery an idol of a calf that made a lowing sound.
phrases.explanation: While Moses was away on Mount Sinai communing with his Lord, the Children of Israel took the golden ornaments they had borrowed from Pharaoh’s people and cast from them the body of a calf fashioned by al-Samiri that produced a lowing sound like a bull.

phrases.translation: Did they not see that it could neither speak to them nor guide them to the ˹Right˺ Path? Still they took it as a god and were wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: Rebuking their folly, Allah asks whether they could not see that this lifeless calf could neither speak a word to them nor guide them to any path of good or safety, yet they still took it as a god beside Allah and wronged their own souls.

phrases.translation: Later, when they were filled with remorse and realized they had gone astray,
phrases.explanation: When Moses returned and exposed the falsehood of their idol, the calf-worshippers were struck with biting regret and grief, described idiomatically as biting their hands in remorse, and saw clearly that they had strayed far from the truth. True repentance begins when excuses fall away and sinners recognize the gravity of their error.

phrases.translation: they cried, “If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us, we will certainly be losers.”
phrases.explanation: Recognizing the enormity of their sin, they confessed in humble repentance that unless their Lord showed them mercy by accepting their repentance and forgave their worship of the calf, they would surely be among the doomed losers who perish. Only Allah’s mercy and forgiveness can rescue a sinner from the ruin his own hands have wrought.

phrases.translation: Upon Moses’ return to his people, ˹totally˺ furious and sorrowful, he said, “What an evil thing you committed in my absence! Did you want to hasten your Lord’s torment?”
phrases.explanation: When Moses returned from Mount Sinai to his people filled with righteous fury for Allah’s sake and deep sorrow over their fall into idolatry, he condemned the evil way they had acted after his departure and asked why they had rushed ahead instead of waiting patiently for their Lord’s decree.

phrases.translation: Then he threw down the Tablets and grabbed his brother by the hair, dragging him closer.
phrases.explanation: Overwhelmed by anger at seeing them around the calf, Moses cast down the Tablets of the Torah and seized his brother Aaron by the hair of his head and beard, pulling him toward himself on the assumption that Aaron had fallen short in stopping them.

phrases.translation: Aaron pleaded, “O son of my mother! The people overpowered me and were about to kill me. So do not ˹humiliate me and˺ make my enemies rejoice, nor count me among the wrongdoing people.”
phrases.explanation: Appealing tenderly to Moses by reminding him of their shared mother, Aaron explained that the calf-worshippers had deemed him weak and nearly killed him when he opposed them, and begged Moses not to humiliate him to the delight of their enemies or treat him like the idolatrous wrongdoers.

phrases.translation: Moses prayed, “My Lord! Forgive me and my brother!
phrases.explanation: Once Aaron explained that the calf-worshippers had overpowered him and nearly killed him, Moses realized his brother was innocent of their sin and prayed to his Lord to forgive his own hasty anger in seizing Aaron and to forgive Aaron as well. Even righteous zeal requires seeking Allah’s pardon when it leads to harshness toward a brother.

phrases.translation: And admit us into Your mercy. You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.”
phrases.explanation: Moses further beseeched Allah to admit both himself and his brother Aaron into the shelter of His special mercy, praising Allah as the Most Merciful of all who show mercy toward repentant servants. True brotherhood in faith ends every misunderstanding by turning together toward divine compassion.

phrases.translation: Those who worshipped the calf will certainly be afflicted with Allah’s wrath as well as disgrace in the life of this world.
phrases.explanation: Allah decrees that those who took the golden calf as a god will inevitably be overtaken by severe wrath from their Lord, through the command that they slay one another in repentance, along with lasting humiliation and abasement in the life of this world. Turning from the Creator to a lifeless idol brings both spiritual and worldly disgrace.

phrases.translation: This is how We reward those who invent falsehood
phrases.explanation: With such wrath and humiliation does Allah requite everyone who fabricates lies against Him and invents false objects of worship or religious innovations without divine authority. The punishment of the calf-worshippers thus stands as a permanent warning against every form of invented falsehood in religion.

phrases.translation: But those who commit evil, then repent and become ˹true˺ believers,
phrases.explanation: Right after declaring the punishment of those who invented the calf, Allah opens the door of hope for those who committed evil deeds of idolatry or disobedience and then turned back to Allah in sincere remorse and believed in His signs. No sin is beyond pardon when followed by genuine repentance and faith.

phrases.translation: your Lord will certainly be All-Forgiving, Most-Merciful
phrases.explanation: After such sincere repentance and return to faith, the Lord is truly All-Forgiving toward their past sins by erasing their guilt and Most Merciful toward them by sparing them punishment. Divine mercy welcomes back even those who fell into grave error once they sincerely mend their ways.

phrases.translation: When Moses’ anger subsided, he took up the Tablets
phrases.explanation: Once Moses’ intense fury at his people’s worship of the calf calmed down and his heart grew still, he picked up the Tablets of the Torah that he had cast onto the ground in righteous indignation. Calmness restored his focus to the sacred trust of revelation.

phrases.translation: whose text contained guidance and mercy for those who stand in awe of their Lord
phrases.explanation: In the written text inscribed upon those Tablets were clear guidance to the straight path and divine mercy for those who fear their Lord and dread His punishment with reverent awe. Scripture yields its full blessing of guidance and mercy to hearts humbled by reverence for Allah.

phrases.translation: Moses chose seventy men from among his people for Our appointment and, when they were seized by an earthquake,
phrases.explanation: At Allah’s command Moses selected seventy of the finest elders of the Children of Israel to accompany him to Mount Sinai at the appointed time to apologize for their people’s worship of the calf, but when they demanded to see Allah openly, a violent convulsion struck them down dead. Even the elite of the community perished when they overstepped proper reverence.

phrases.translation: he cried, “My Lord! Had You willed, You could have destroyed them long ago, and me as well. Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done?
phrases.explanation: Standing alone in distress over their death, Moses pleaded that if Allah had willed He could have destroyed both them and him before this journey, and asked in humble supplication whether Allah would destroy the whole community on account of the sins committed by the ignorant fools among them.

phrases.translation: This is only a test from You—by which You allow whoever you will to stray and guide whoever You will.
phrases.explanation: Moses acknowledged that the trial of the calf and what befell his people was nothing other than a test and decree from Allah, whereby He lets stray whomever He wills and guides to the truth whomever He wills. Recognizing Allah’s absolute sovereignty over guidance and trial deepened Moses’ humility in prayer.

phrases.translation: You are our Guardian. So forgive us and have mercy on us. You are the best forgiver
phrases.explanation: Confessing that Allah alone was their Protector and Helper with no guardian beside Him, Moses beseeched Allah to forgive their sins and encompass them with mercy, praising Him as the best of all who forgive. In response to his plea, Allah restored the seventy elders to life.

phrases.translation: Ordain for us what is good in this life and the next. Indeed, we have turned to You ˹in repentance˺.”
phrases.explanation: Continuing his supplication, Moses asked Allah to decree for them what is good in this world through righteous obedience and wellbeing, and what is good in the hereafter through forgiveness and Paradise, declaring that they had turned back to Allah in sincere repentance. Seeking the good of both worlds is the comprehensive prayer of those who turn back to Allah.

phrases.translation: Allah replied, “I will inflict My torment on whoever I will. But My mercy encompasses everything.
phrases.explanation: Answering Moses’ prayer, Allah declared that He afflicts with His punishment whomever He wills among the rebellious, whereas His mercy encompasses all things in creation in this world and is specially reserved for the believers in the hereafter. Divine punishment falls by justice, while divine mercy overflows across creation by grace.

phrases.translation: I will ordain mercy for those who shun evil, pay alms-tax, and believe in Our revelations
phrases.explanation: Allah announced that in the hereafter He will decree His everlasting mercy specifically for those who guard themselves against idolatry and major sins, purify their wealth and souls by paying the obligatory alms-tax, and believe in all of His revealed signs. Lasting mercy in the hereafter belongs to those who join reverence with charity and faith.

phrases.translation: “˹They are˺ the ones who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whose description they find in their Torah and the Gospel.
phrases.explanation: Completing the description of those for whom Allah decrees His encompassing mercy, Allah identifies them as those who follow the Messenger Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet of Mecca who neither read nor wrote from human books, whose attributes and mission they find written down with them in the Torah and the Gospel.

phrases.translation: He commands them to do good and forbids them from evil, permits for them what is lawful and forbids to them what is impure,
phrases.explanation: This Prophet commands people to follow every moral good including pure monotheism and obedience, forbids every evil of idolatry and sin, makes lawful for them the wholesome foods that pre-Islamic custom or earlier severe laws had restricted, and prohibits foul things such as carrion, blood, and swine.

phrases.translation: and relieves them from their burdens and the shackles that bound them.
phrases.explanation: Through his merciful law, Allah lifts from believers the heavy burdens and harsh legal restrictions that had bound earlier communities like iron collars, such as cutting away impure skin, burning war spoils, or executing a sinner as the only form of repentance. Islam replaces the punitive legal yokes of earlier dispensations with a balanced, merciful law.

phrases.translation: ˹Only˺ those who believe in him, honour and support him, and follow the light sent down to him will be successful.”
phrases.explanation: Therefore, those who believe in the Prophet Muhammad, revere and honour him, assist him against his enemies, and follow the clear light of the Quran sent down with him are the ones who will attain true, everlasting success in both worlds. True salvation for People of the Book and all others lies in embracing and supporting this final Messenger.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O humanity! I am Allah’s Messenger to you all.
phrases.explanation: Confirming the universality of his mission just mentioned to Moses, Allah commands the Prophet Muhammad to proclaim to all humanity, Arabs and non-Arabs as well as Jews and Christians alike, that he is Allah’s Messenger sent to every one of them without exception. Unlike earlier prophets sent to specific nations, Muhammad was sent as Allah’s Messenger to all mankind.

phrases.translation: To Him ˹alone˺ belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. He gives life and causes death.”
phrases.explanation: The One who sent him is Allah, to whom alone belongs the absolute dominion of the heavens and the earth, besides whom no deity deserves worship, and who alone brings creatures to life from nothing and causes them to die. The One who holds universal dominion and the power of life and death alone has the right to send a universal Messenger.

phrases.translation: So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, who believes in Allah and His revelations. And follow him, so you may be ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: All people are therefore commanded to believe in Allah and in His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet who himself believes in Allah and in all of Allah’s revealed words and Scriptures, and to follow his guidance so that they may walk the straight path. Following the unlettered Prophet is the sole path to right guidance because his message comes purely from Allah.

phrases.translation: There are some among the people of Moses who guide with the truth
phrases.explanation: Though many among the Children of Israel fell into rebellion, Allah praises an upright community among the people of Moses who guide people by the clear truth and embrace the prophetic mission foretold in their Scripture. Fairness requires acknowledging the righteous minority within an otherwise wayward nation.

phrases.translation: and establish justice accordingly
phrases.explanation: Whenever they judge between people or apply religious law, this upright group establishes fair and impartial justice in strict accordance with the truth rather than twisting rulings for bribes or partisan interest. True guidance in belief naturally produces equity in judgment. True fidelity to revelation is proved when a community judges fairly even against its own desires.

phrases.translation: We divided them into twelve tribes—each as a community.
phrases.explanation: Recalling His favours upon the Children of Israel in the wilderness, Allah states that He organized them into twelve distinct tribes descended from the twelve sons of Jacob, each tribe forming an ordered community under its own appointed leader. Distinct tribal organization preserved social order while uniting them under one prophetic law.

phrases.translation: And We revealed to Moses, when his people asked for water, “Strike the rock with your staff.” Then twelve springs gushed out. Each tribe knew its drinking place.
phrases.explanation: When they suffered thirst in the Sinai desert and asked Moses for water, Allah revealed to him to strike the stone with his staff, whereupon twelve abundant springs gushed forth so that each of the twelve tribes knew its own separate watering place without crowding or strife.

phrases.translation: We shaded them with clouds and sent down to them manna and quails, ˹saying˺, “Eat from the good things We have provided for you.”
phrases.explanation: In the shadeless heat of the wilderness Allah spread white clouds above them for cool shade and sent down sweet manna and plump quails effortlessly for their sustenance, bidding them to eat gratefully of the wholesome provisions He had granted them. Shade from the desert sun and effortless food from heaven left them with every reason for gratitude.

phrases.translation: They ˹certainly˺ did not wrong Us, but wronged themselves
phrases.explanation: When they later met those extraordinary miracles with ingratitude and disobedience, they did not diminish or harm Allah in the least, but rather wronged their own souls by forfeiting His blessing and incurring His wrath. Human rebellion never diminishes Allah’s sovereignty, but only strips the rebels of the blessings they enjoyed.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when it was said to them, “Enter this city ˹of Jerusalem˺ and eat from wherever you please.
phrases.explanation: Allah reminds them of when their forefathers were commanded after the wilderness years to enter and dwell in the holy town, identified by commentators as Jerusalem or Jericho, and to eat freely of its abundant fruits and provisions wherever they wished. Entering the promised land after years of wandering was a gift requiring humble thankfulness.

phrases.translation: Say, ‘Absolve us,’ and enter the gate with humility. We will forgive your sins, ˹and˺ We will multiply the reward for the good-doers.”
phrases.explanation: As a sign of gratitude upon entering, they were commanded to ask for forgiveness by saying a word of absolution and to pass through the city gate bowing low in humility, with Allah promising to forgive their errors and multiply the reward of the righteous.

phrases.translation: But the wrongdoers among them changed the words they were commanded to say.
phrases.explanation: Instead of obeying humbly, the wrongdoers among them mocked the divine command by distorting the prescribed word of repentance into a scoffing phrase meaning a grain of wheat in a hair, while creeping through the gate on their buttocks in insolent derision. Turning a sacred formula of repentance into a vulgar joke revealed deep contempt for divine command.

phrases.translation: So We sent down a punishment from the heavens upon them for their wrongdoing
phrases.explanation: Because they persistently transgressed and mocked Allah’s command, Allah sent down upon them a devastating plague and torment from heaven that swept away tens of thousands of the wrongdoers in a single hour. Mocking Allah’s words at the very moment of receiving His favour brought swift retribution from heaven.

phrases.translation: Ask them ˹O Prophet˺ about ˹the people of˺ the town which was by the sea, who broke the Sabbath.
phrases.explanation: To expose the hidden history of disobedience among the forefathers of the Jews around Medina, Allah instructs the Prophet to ask them about the inhabitants of the coastal town of Aylah on the Red Sea, who transgressed the sanctity of the Sabbath after being forbidden to work or fish on Saturdays.

phrases.translation: During the Sabbath, ˹abundant˺ fish would come to them clearly visible, but on other days the fish were never seen. In this way We tested them for their rebelliousness
phrases.explanation: On Saturdays the fish would swim up to the shore in huge numbers, floating openly on the surface within easy reach, whereas once the Sabbath ended the fish vanished into the deep until the next Saturday, a severe test by which Allah tried them because of their prior disobedience.

phrases.translation: When some of ˹the righteous among˺ them questioned ˹their fellow Sabbath-keepers˺, “Why do you ˹bother to˺ warn those ˹Sabbath-breakers˺ who will either be destroyed or severely punished by Allah?”
phrases.explanation: When the Sabbath-breakers dug channels and set traps on Friday to catch the Saturday fish, the town split into three groups, and one group who abstained from the sin asked the preachers why they kept admonishing a people whom Allah was surely going to destroy or punish severely.

phrases.translation: They replied, “Just to be free from your Lord’s blame, and so perhaps they may abstain.”
phrases.explanation: The righteous preachers answered that they continued forbidding the evil for two reasons: first, to fulfill their duty of admonition and have a valid excuse before their Lord, and second, in the hope that the sinners might fear Allah and abandon their transgression. Forbidding evil both clears the conscience of the righteous before Allah and keeps the door of repentance open.

phrases.translation: When they ignored the warning they were given, We rescued those who used to warn against evil
phrases.explanation: When the Sabbath-breakers stubbornly disregarded every admonition and refused to give up their unlawful fishing schemes, Allah delivered the righteous believers who had actively forbidden their evil from the impending catastrophe. When collective punishment falls on a corrupt town, Allah saves those who actively opposed the sin.

phrases.translation: and overtook the wrongdoers with a dreadful punishment for their rebelliousness
phrases.explanation: At the same time Allah seized the wrongdoers who had violated the sanctity of the Sabbath with a wretched, humiliating torment as a just recompense for their persistent rebellion against His command. Clever legal tricks designed to bypass Allah’s clear prohibitions only make the resulting punishment more severe.

phrases.translation: But when they stubbornly persisted in violation, We said to them, “Be disgraced apes!”
phrases.explanation: When the Sabbath-breakers insolently disdained obeying Allah and refused to desist from what He had forbidden, Allah issued His irresistible command transforming them physically into despised, outcast apes, stripped of human dignity before perishing shortly afterward. Because they behaved with animal greed toward Allah’s sacred limits, their outward form was made to match their inward degradation.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember, O Prophet,˺ when your Lord declared that He would send against them others who would make them suffer terribly until the Day of Judgment.
phrases.explanation: Because of their repeated rebellions, their Lord solemnly declared that He would continue raising against the disobedient among the Children of Israel rulers and nations who would subject them to humiliating domination, tribute, and severe affliction right up to the Day of Resurrection. History bore out this solemn decree as successive powers subjugated them whenever they abandoned Allah’s covenant.

phrases.translation: Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, but He is certainly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Truly, the Lord is swift in executing His punishment upon those who persist in rebellion when His decree arrives, yet He remains All-Forgiving and Most Merciful toward whoever repents, believes, and returns to obedience. Pairing the warning of swift punishment with the promise of forgiveness keeps the door of return open.

phrases.translation: We dispersed them through the land in groups—some were righteous, others were less so.
phrases.explanation: Instead of leaving them united in one realm, Allah scattered the Children of Israel across the earth into separate communities, among whom are righteous believers who obey Allah’s truth and others who fall short in disbelief and sin. Even within a scattered nation, Allah distinguishes the upright believers from those who persist in disobedience.

phrases.translation: We tested them with prosperity and adversity, so perhaps they would return ˹to the Right Path˺
phrases.explanation: Throughout their dispersion Allah tried them both with periods of ease, wealth, and security and with periods of hardship, humiliation, and distress, so that they might repent of their errors and return to obeying their Lord. Alternating blessings and hardships are designed to awaken reflection and bring wayward hearts back to obedience.

phrases.translation: Then they were succeeded by other generations who inherited the Scripture. They indulged in unlawful gains, claiming, “We will be forgiven ˹after all˺.” And if similar gain came their way, they would seize it.
phrases.explanation: After those earlier generations passed away, degenerate successors inherited the Torah and read its laws, yet sold Allah’s rulings for paltry worldly bribes and illicit gains while presumptuously claiming that Allah would forgive them, even as they stood ready to snatch the next unlawful bribe that came their way.

phrases.translation: Was a covenant not taken from them in the Scripture that they would not say anything about Allah except the truth? And they were already well-versed in its teachings.
phrases.explanation: Rebuking their hypocrisy, Allah asks whether a solemn covenant had not been taken from them in the Torah never to attribute anything to Allah except the truth, especially when they had studied the Book thoroughly and knew that Allah does not forgive those who persist in taking bribes.

phrases.translation: But the ˹eternal˺ Home of the Hereafter is far better for those mindful ˹of Allah˺. Will you not then understand
phrases.explanation: The everlasting abode of Paradise in the hereafter is infinitely better than the paltry worldly goods for which they sold their faith, a reward reserved for those who fear Allah by shunning unlawful gain, if only they would use their reason to understand. A moment’s reflection shows that trading eternal bliss for a fleeting bribe is the worst of bargains.

phrases.translation: As for those who firmly abide by the Scripture and establish prayer
phrases.explanation: In contrast to the corrupt successors who sold the Scripture for bribes, those who hold fast to the true teachings of the Book, affirm the Prophet it foretold, and establish regular prayer in devotion to Allah are praised for their fidelity. Holding fast to Scripture means acting on its commands and establishing prayer rather than merely reciting its words.

phrases.translation: —surely We never discount the reward of those acting righteously
phrases.explanation: Allah assures such faithful servants that He never allows the reward of those who reform their conduct and act righteously to be lost or diminished in the slightest on the Day of Judgment. Righteous reformers never labour in vain before a Lord who preserves every good deed.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when We raised the mountain over them as if it were a cloud and they thought it would fall on them.
phrases.explanation: Recalling another awe-inspiring covenant scene, Allah reminds them of when their forefathers balked at accepting the heavy obligations of the Torah, so Allah uprooted the mountain and suspended it above their heads like a overshadowing canopy until they were certain it would crash down upon them.

phrases.translation: ˹We said,˺ “Hold firmly to that ˹Scripture˺ which We have given you and observe its teachings so perhaps you will become mindful ˹of Allah˺.”
phrases.explanation: Under the shadow of the raised mountain Allah commanded them to accept the Scripture He had given them with firm resolve and to remember and practice the commands and prohibitions within it so that they might guard themselves against His punishment. Even when a covenant is accepted under awe, its purpose is to cultivate lasting mindfulness of Allah.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when your Lord brought forth from the loins of the children of Adam their descendants and had them testify regarding themselves.
