phrases.explanation: Expanding from the covenant of Israel to the universal covenant of all humanity, Allah recalls when He brought forth from the backs of Adam’s descendants all future generations, one generation after another like tiny particles, and made them bear witness regarding their own souls. Every human soul carries an innate, primordial recognition of its Creator implanted before earthly life began.

phrases.translation: ˹Allah asked,˺ “Am I not your Lord?” They replied, “Yes, You are! We testify.”
phrases.explanation: Addressing them directly with innate awareness, Allah asked whether He was not their sole Lord and Creator, and every human soul testified in affirmation that He alone is their Lord with no god or partner beside Him. This universal testimony establishes monotheism as the original truth of human nature rather than a foreign invention.

phrases.translation: ˹He cautioned,˺ “Now you have no right to say on Judgment Day, ‘We were not aware of this.’
phrases.explanation: This primordial testimony was taken and reinforced by natural human disposition and sent messengers so that idolaters could never plead on the Day of Resurrection that they had been unaware of Allah’s exclusive lordship and oneness. On Judgment Day no one will be able to claim that monotheism was an unfamiliar demand.

phrases.translation: Nor say, ‘It was our forefathers who had associated others ˹with Allah in worship˺ and we, as their descendants, followed in their footsteps.
phrases.explanation: That covenant also blocks polytheists from excusing themselves on Judgment Day by claiming that it was their forefathers before them who invented idol worship while they were merely later descendants who grew up imitating their ancestors. Inherited culture and ancestral custom cannot override the primordial covenant each soul made with its Creator.

phrases.translation: Will you then destroy us for the falsehood they invented?’”
phrases.explanation: Having already testified to Allah’s oneness in their primordial nature and received the warnings of messengers, they will have no right to ask whether Allah will punish them for the false religion founded by earlier liars. Following predecessors into idolatry is a conscious choice for which every generation remains accountable.

phrases.translation: This is how We make our signs clear,
phrases.explanation: Just as Allah explained the history of past nations and the primordial covenant taken from Adam’s descendants, so does He set forth His signs, proofs, and verses in full clarity throughout the Quran. Divine revelation leaves no essential truth obscure. Clear exposition of both history and human nature removes every excuse for persisting in error.

phrases.translation: so perhaps they will return ˹to the Right Path˺
phrases.explanation: Allah sets forth these clear proofs and reminders in order that those who have strayed into idolatry or heedlessness may reflect upon them, abandon their falsehood, and return to the truth of pure monotheism. The ultimate aim of every Quranic proof is to guide wandering hearts back to their Lord.

phrases.translation: And relate to them ˹O Prophet˺ the story of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he abandoned them,
phrases.explanation: Allah commands the Prophet to recite to his people the cautionary account of a man, identified in early commentary mostly with Balaam son of Beor or with Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt, whom Allah had granted knowledge of His revealed signs and sacred names, yet who stripped himself of them like a snake shedding its skin by rejecting faith.

phrases.translation: so Satan took hold of him, and he became a deviant
phrases.explanation: Once he cast off obedience to the revelations he knew, Satan overtook him and made him his follower, so that despite his former learning he ended up among the ruined deviants who strayed into destruction. Religious knowledge that is not practiced in humble obedience becomes a cause of ruin rather than salvation.

phrases.translation: If We had willed, We would have elevated him with Our signs, but he clung to this life—following his evil desires.
phrases.explanation: Had Allah willed to grant him success, He would have raised him to high honour through acting upon the signs he had been given, but instead he inclined heavily toward the fleeting goods of the lowly world and followed his own base desires against Allah’s command.

phrases.translation: His example is that of a dog: if you chase it away, it pants, and if you leave it, it ˹still˺ pants.
phrases.explanation: Because of his insatiable greed for the world and imperviousness to admonition, his likeness in humiliation is that of a dog whose tongue hangs out panting whether you drive it away with a shout or leave it alone, just as this scholar remained consumed by worldly craving whether warned or left unwarned.

phrases.translation: This is the example of the people who deny Our signs. So narrate ˹to them˺ stories ˹of the past˺, so perhaps they will reflect
phrases.explanation: Such degraded spiritual panting is the likeness of all people who deny Allah’s signs after truth has reached them, so Allah instructs the Prophet to relate these historical lessons so that listeners may ponder and take heed. Recounting the fall of learned men who sold their faith warns every reader to guard his heart.

phrases.translation: What an evil example of those who denied Our signs!
phrases.explanation: How wretched and disgraceful is the likeness of the people who denied Allah’s clear revelations and proofs after knowledge came to them, being compared to a panting dog enslaved by base appetite. Trading divine wisdom for worldly craving reduces a person to the lowest state.

phrases.translation: They ˹only˺ wronged their own souls
phrases.explanation: By rejecting Allah’s clear signs and following their base desires, they did not harm Allah or diminish His dominion at all, but continuously wronged and ruined their own souls by earning eternal disgrace in the hereafter. Rejecting clear truth harms only the denier, who trades everlasting honour for self-inflicted ruin.

phrases.translation: Whoever Allah guides is truly guided.
phrases.explanation: Whoever Allah guides to faith and obedience through His grace is the one truly guided to the straight path of salvation, and no tempter can lead him astray. True guidance is a gift of divine favour rather than mere human cleverness. No obstacle can misguide a heart that Allah has graciously directed to the truth.

phrases.translation: And whoever He leaves to stray, they are the ˹true˺ losers
phrases.explanation: Conversely, whoever Allah forsakes and leaves to stray because of his preference for blindness over truth will find no guide beside Him, and such people are the true losers who have forfeited their souls and eternal bliss. Being forsaken to one’s own desires is the greatest loss a human being can suffer.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We have destined many jinn and humans for Hell. They have hearts they do not understand with, eyes they do not see with, and ears they do not hear with.
phrases.explanation: Allah declares that He has created and destined for Hellfire many among the jinn and mankind who possess hearts with which they refuse to comprehend the truth, eyes with which they refuse to see Allah’s signs, and ears with which they refuse to hear divine admonition.

phrases.translation: They are like cattle. In fact, they are even less guided! Such ˹people˺ are ˹entirely˺ heedless
phrases.explanation: In failing to use their faculties for guidance, they are like grazing livestock that care only for food and drink. indeed, they are even further astray than cattle, because animals obey their Creator and know their way home, whereas these heedless people ignore the very purpose of their creation.

phrases.translation: Allah has the Most Beautiful Names. So call upon Him by them,
phrases.explanation: To Allah alone belong the Most Beautiful Names that express His supreme perfection, majesty, and mercy, such as the All-Merciful, the All-Knowing, and the Almighty, so believers are commanded to call upon Him and praise Him by those sacred names. Invoking Allah by His Beautiful Names aligns the servant’s heart with His majesty, wisdom, and grace.

phrases.translation: and keep away from those who abuse His Names. They will be punished for what they used to do
phrases.explanation: Believers must turn away from the polytheists and heretics who deviate regarding Allah’s Names, such as deriving the idol names al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat from Allah’s names or denying their true meanings, for Allah will surely requite them for their fabrications. Distorting sacred names to legitimise idols or strip Allah of His attributes will be answered with just punishment.

phrases.translation: And among those We created is a group that guides with the truth
phrases.explanation: In contrast to those created for Hell who neglect their faculties, Allah affirms that among the human beings He created is a blessed community, specifically identified in prophetic reports with the upright followers of Muhammad, who call people to the truth. In every age Allah preserves a community that upholds pure truth amidst surrounding error.

phrases.translation: and establishes justice accordingly
phrases.explanation: This guided community not only summons others to the truth of revelation, but also governs and judges fairly by that truth in every dispute, never swerving into tyranny or partiality. Sound belief and just governance go hand in hand among those truly guided by Allah.

phrases.translation: As for those who deny Our signs, We will gradually draw them to destruction
phrases.explanation: As for those who reject Allah’s revelations and messengers, Allah warns that He will draw them step by step toward ruin by opening for them the gates of worldly wealth, health, and abundance every time they commit a fresh sin. Worldly abundance granted to unrepentant deniers is a gradual trap rather than a sign of divine pleasure.

phrases.translation: in ways they cannot comprehend
phrases.explanation: Because each new sin is met with fresh worldly prosperity instead of immediate punishment, they are deceived into thinking they are favoured and do not realize that this respite is leading them directly to sudden destruction. When prosperity blinds sinners to their own peril, destruction overtakes them from where they least expect.

phrases.translation: I ˹only˺ delay their end for a while, but My planning is flawless
phrases.explanation: Allah declares that He grants those deniers a long respite and extends their worldly lifespans so they may sink deeper into rebellion, for His subtle plan against the arrogant is firm, unbreakable, and impossible for any sinner to escape when the appointed hour strikes. Long respite never means that Allah has forgotten the wrongdoers or that His plan can be defeated.

phrases.translation: Have they not ever given it a thought? Their fellow man is not insane.
phrases.explanation: Rebuking the Meccan polytheists who slandered Muhammad as possessed, Allah asks why they do not pause to reflect with sound reason and recognize that their lifelong companion, whose honesty and wisdom they know firsthand, has no trace of madness at all. Decades of known truthfulness and sound judgment proved to Quraysh that the Prophet was completely free of madness.

phrases.translation: He is only sent with a clear warning
phrases.explanation: Far from being insane as his detractors claimed, he is nothing other than a plain, truthful warner sent by Allah to alert them openly before an inescapable punishment overtakes them for their idolatry. His earnest warnings flowed from prophetic compassion to save his people before the final judgment arrived.

phrases.translation: Have they ever reflected on the wonders of the heavens and the earth, and everything Allah has created,
phrases.explanation: Allah urges the deniers to look with reflection at the vast dominion and sovereign kingdom of the heavens and the earth and at all the varied things Allah has created within them, which testify unmistakably to the oneness and power of their Creator. Every level of the cosmos points unmistakably to the wisdom and unity of its Maker.

phrases.translation: and that perhaps their end is near? So what message after this ˹Quran˺ would they believe in
phrases.explanation: They should also reflect that their own appointed time of death may already have drawn near, lest they perish in disbelief and enter the Fire, and ask themselves what clearer discourse or warning they could possibly believe in if they reject this Quran. When death may arrive at any moment, postponing faith in the clearest of Scriptures is utter folly.

phrases.translation: Whoever Allah allows to stray, none can guide, leaving them to wander blindly in their defiance
phrases.explanation: Whoever Allah decrees to go astray because of his stubborn rejection of the truth has no helper able to guide him to the right path, and Allah leaves such people wandering in confusion and blindness within their own insolent rebellion. Once a person chooses defiance over guidance, no human argument can rescue him from his confusion.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ regarding the Hour, “When will it be?” Say, “That knowledge is only with my Lord. He alone will reveal it when the time comes.
phrases.explanation: When the polytheists of Quraysh or the Jews asked the Prophet in challenge or curiosity when the Final Hour of Resurrection would take place, Allah instructed him to reply that knowledge of its exact time belongs exclusively to his Lord, and none besides Him can manifest it at its appointed time.

phrases.translation: It is too tremendous for the heavens and the earth and will only take you by surprise.”
phrases.explanation: Both the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth find the terror and hidden knowledge of the Hour weighty and overwhelming, and when it finally arrives it will come upon people only suddenly and unawares. Keeping the exact timing of the Hour hidden ensures that people remain watchful at every moment.

phrases.translation: They ask you as if you had full knowledge of it. Say, “That knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know.”
phrases.explanation: They persist in questioning the Prophet about the Hour as though he were eagerly pryed into its hidden secret or specially privy to it, so he is commanded to repeat that its knowledge rests solely with Allah, though most people do not realize why Allah keeps its timing concealed.

phrases.translation: Say, “I have no power to benefit or protect myself, except by the Will of Allah.
phrases.explanation: Demonstrating his complete servitude before Allah, the Prophet is commanded to declare that he possesses no independent power to bring benefit to himself or ward off harm from his own person except whatever Allah wills for him. If the noblest of messengers depends wholly on Allah for benefit and protection, no creature can claim independent power.

phrases.translation: If I had known the unknown, I would have benefited myself enormously, and no harm would have ever touched me.
phrases.explanation: Had he possessed knowledge of the unseen on his own, he would have amassed abundant good and provisions in advance for every lean year and guarded himself beforehand so that no adversity, injury, or hardship ever touched him. The trials and hardships the Prophet endured in his own life proved that unseen knowledge belongs to Allah alone.

phrases.translation: I am only a warner and deliverer of good news for those who believe.”
phrases.explanation: Instead of claiming divine knowledge of the unseen, he declares that he is solely a servant sent as a warner against Allah’s punishment and a bearer of glad tidings of Paradise for a people who believe in his message. Recognizing the Prophet’s true role as warner and herald directs faith toward those who heed his call.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who created you from a single soul, then from it made its spouse so he may find comfort in her.
phrases.explanation: Returning to the proof of Allah’s exclusive right to worship, the verse reminds humanity that Allah alone created them all from a single soul, Adam, and created from him his wife Eve of his own kind so that he might find intimacy, tranquility, and companionship with her.

phrases.translation: After he had been united with her, she carried a light burden that developed gradually.
phrases.explanation: When the husband united with his wife in marital intimacy, she conceived a light initial pregnancy of sperm that caused her no heavy distress as she went about and rose and sat during its early stage. The quiet, hidden beginning of human life in the womb unfolds entirely under Allah’s care.

phrases.translation: When it grew heavy, they prayed to Allah, their Lord, “If you grant us good offspring, we will certainly be grateful.”
phrases.explanation: When the child grew large in her womb and she became heavy and anxious as delivery approached, the two parents supplicated Allah their Lord, vowing that if He granted them a sound, healthy human child they would surely be grateful to Him. Anxious need before childbirth naturally drives human beings to call upon their true Creator alone.

phrases.translation: But when He granted their descendants good offspring, they associated false gods in what He has given them.
phrases.explanation: Yet when Allah granted them a sound, healthy child, partners were associated with Allah regarding the gift He alone had bestowed, explained by early commentators either through the narrative of naming a child Abd al-Harith after Satan’s repeated whispers or through the Arab polytheists dedicating their children to idols.

phrases.translation: Exalted is Allah above what they associate ˹with Him˺
phrases.explanation: High and transcendent is Allah above every false partner, idol, and co-sharer that the polytheists associate with Him in worship or in naming the children whom He alone created and formed in the womb. Allah’s creative power and supreme sovereignty stand infinitely above all the false partners that people invent.

phrases.translation: Do they associate ˹with Allah˺ those ˹idols˺ which cannot create anything,
phrases.explanation: Exposing the absurdity of polytheism, Allah asks how people can set up as partners in worship alongside the Creator lifeless idols and false deities that have no power to create even the smallest thing in existence. The power to create from nothing is the unmistakable mark separating the true God from false deities.

phrases.translation: but are in fact created
phrases.explanation: Far from creating anything, those idols are themselves created objects fashioned and carved by human hands out of stone, wood, or metal, utterly dependent on the One who made both them and their worshippers. Worshipping an object manufactured by human hands is an inversion of human dignity and reason.

phrases.translation: which cannot help them, or even help themselves
phrases.explanation: Those carved idols possess no power to bring any victory, aid, or relief to the polytheists who worship them when calamity strikes, nor can they even defend or help their own stone bodies if someone comes to break or disgrace them. A deity that cannot even protect its own statue from being smashed can never rescue its worshippers.

phrases.translation: And if you ˹idolaters˺ call upon them for guidance, they cannot respond to you.
phrases.explanation: If the idolaters call upon their false gods to guide them to the right path or direct them in any matter of need, those lifeless statues cannot follow their call or respond with any guidance at all. Seeking moral or spiritual direction from mute stone is the height of futility.

phrases.translation: It is all the same whether you call them or remain silent
phrases.explanation: Because carved idols neither hear nor understand a single word spoken to them, it makes no difference whatsoever whether their worshippers cry out to them in earnest supplication or remain completely silent before them. Loud prayers and silent neglect receive the exact same non-response from lifeless statues of stone.

phrases.translation: Those ˹idols˺ you invoke besides Allah are created beings like yourselves.
phrases.explanation: All the false deities that polytheists invoke besides Allah are themselves owned, subjugated creatures under Allah’s dominion just as human beings are His servants, possessing no share of lordship. Elevating fellow creatures or carved objects to divine status violates the shared servitude of all creation.

phrases.translation: So call upon them and see if they will answer you, if your claims are true
phrases.explanation: Allah challenges the polytheists to call upon those idols in their distress and see whether the statues can answer their prayers, if their claim that these idols are gods worthy of worship is true. The total silence of the idols when called upon exposes the emptiness of polytheism.

phrases.translation: Do they have feet to walk with? Or hands to hold with? Or eyes to see with? Or ears to hear with?
phrases.explanation: Demonstrating that carved idols are inferior even to the humans who worship them, Allah asks whether these statues have feet to walk with, hands to grasp or defend with, eyes to see with, or ears to hear their worshippers’ prayers, when in truth they lack even the basic faculties of living creatures.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Call upon your associate-gods and conspire against me without delay
phrases.explanation: Confident that lifeless idols can do nothing, the Prophet is commanded to challenge the polytheists to summon all their alleged partner-gods together and plot every scheme they can against him without granting him a single moment’s delay. One prophet’s fearless challenge to all the idols of Arabia proved their complete impotence.

phrases.translation: “Indeed, my Protector is Allah Who has revealed this Book.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet declares that he has no fear of their idols or their plots because his Guardian, Helper, and Protector is Allah alone, who sent down the Quran to him with truth and authority. He who stands under the protection of the Almighty has no reason to fear the schemes of creatures.

phrases.translation: For He ˹alone˺ protects the righteous
phrases.explanation: Allah Himself takes charge of protecting, supporting, and defending His righteous servants who obey His commands and worship Him alone, so no conspiracy of idolaters or false gods can ever overcome them. Righteous obedience places a believing servant under the direct, unfailing guardianship of the Sovereign Lord of the worlds.

phrases.translation: But those ˹false gods˺ you call besides Him can neither help you nor even themselves.”
phrases.explanation: In contrast to Allah’s unfailing protection of the righteous, all the false gods that the idolaters invoke besides Him are utterly powerless either to aid their worshippers against Allah’s decree or even to defend themselves from harm. Repeating the helplessness of false gods drives home the contrast with Allah’s living guardianship.

phrases.translation: If you ˹idolaters˺ call them to guidance, they cannot hear.
phrases.explanation: Even if the polytheists call upon their idols to guide them or listen to their pleas, the lifeless statues have no hearing with which to perceive a single word addressed to them. Deafness to every plea proves that idols lack the most basic attribute of a deity.

phrases.translation: And you ˹O Prophet˺ may see them facing towards you, but they cannot see
phrases.explanation: And although an onlooker sees these carved images with sculpted eyes facing directly toward him as if looking at him, they possess no sight at all and cannot see anything before them. Painted or carved eyes give only the illusion of sight while seeing nothing at all.

phrases.translation: Be gracious, enjoin what is right, and turn away from those who act ignorantly
phrases.explanation: Training the Prophet in noble character, Allah commands him to accept what comes easily from people’s conduct and pardon their shortcomings, to enjoin every recognized moral good and obedience to Allah, and to turn away with patient forbearance from the abuse of ignorant fools without retaliating in kind.

phrases.translation: If you are tempted by Satan, then seek refuge with Allah.
phrases.explanation: Whenever a whisper or provocation from Satan stirs up anger in the heart to turn the Prophet away from pardoning the ignorant and responding with forbearance, he is commanded to seek refuge immediately with Allah from Satan’s incitement. Turning immediately to Allah in refuge extinguishes the spark of anger before Satan can fan it into sin.

phrases.translation: Surely He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: Truly, Allah is All-Hearing of both the foolish abuse of the ignorant and the believer’s prayer for refuge, and All-Knowing of what repels Satan’s whispers and protects the hearts of His servants. Confidence that Allah hears every insult and knows every heart makes patient forbearance possible.

phrases.translation: Indeed, when Satan whispers to those mindful ˹of Allah˺, they remember ˹their Lord˺
phrases.explanation: When a sudden temptation, impulse of anger, or whisper from Satan touches those who fear Allah and guard His limits, they do not persist in heedlessness, but immediately remember Allah’s command, His punishment, and His reward. Mindfulness of Allah does not mean never being tempted, but remembering Him as soon as temptation strikes.

phrases.translation: then they start to see ˹things˺ clearly
phrases.explanation: As soon as the God-fearing remember their Lord, the fog of temptation lifts from their hearts and they see clearly where truth and obedience lie, recognizing Satan’s trap and returning at once to upright conduct. Sincere remembrance of Allah restores moral clarity and breaks the deceptive spell of Satan’s whispers.

phrases.translation: But the devils persistently plunge their ˹human˺ associates deeper into wickedness, sparing no effort
phrases.explanation: Unlike the God-fearing who remember Allah and recover their sight, the human followers and brothers of the devils are dragged ever deeper into error, blindness, and rebellion by the satans, who never slacken in inciting them nor do the sinners cease obeying them. Persistent partnership between devils and unrepentant sinners drags the heedless ever further from salvation.

phrases.translation: If you ˹O Prophet˺ do not bring them a sign ˹which they demanded˺, they ask, “Why do you not make it yourself?”
phrases.explanation: Whenever the Prophet did not bring the Meccan polytheists a specific miracle or verse that they stubbornly demanded, they mockingly asked why he did not invent, fabricate, or select one by himself on the spot. Treating revelation as something a prophet could invent on demand showed their ignorance of prophethood.

phrases.translation: Say, “I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord.
phrases.explanation: Allah commands him to reply that a prophet has no right to invent verses or produce miracles at his own whim, for he follows solely what is revealed to him from his Lord. Strict fidelity to revealed words is the proof that the Messenger speaks for Allah rather than himself.

phrases.translation: This ˹Quran˺ is an insight from your Lord—a guide and a mercy for those who believe.”
phrases.explanation: Instead of the arbitrary signs they demand, this Quran itself is a treasury of clear proofs and inner insights from their Lord, serving as unerring guidance and saving mercy for a people who believe. For hearts open to truth, the Quran’s own light and wisdom surpass every demanded spectacle.

phrases.translation: When the Quran is recited, listen to it attentively and be silent,
phrases.explanation: When the Quran is recited, explained by early commentators primarily regarding the congregational prayer behind the imam as well as the sermon and public recitation, believers are commanded to lend an attentive ear to its words and remain silent so they can understand its message. Respectful silence and attentive listening during recitation honour the speech of the Creator.

phrases.translation: so you may be shown mercy
phrases.explanation: Listening attentively and keeping respectful silence when Allah’s Book is recited prepares the heart to absorb its guidance and makes the listener worthy of receiving Allah’s encompassing mercy in both worlds. Divine mercy descends upon those who quiet their voices and open their hearts to the Quran.

phrases.translation: Remember your Lord inwardly with humility and reverence and in a moderate tone of voice, both morning and evening.
phrases.explanation: Believers are commanded to remember their Lord within their own souls in humble submission and reverent fear of Him, speaking quietly in a moderate tone below loud shouting in the morning and the evening. Inward sincerity and gentle moderation in voice keep remembrance pure of ostentation.

phrases.translation: And do not be one of the heedless
phrases.explanation: By maintaining regular, humble remembrance of Allah at both ends of the day in the morning and evening, a servant guards himself from becoming one of the heedless whose hearts neglect their Creator. Anchoring the start and close of every day in remembrance keeps the believer’s heart awake and mindful.

phrases.translation: Surely those ˹angels˺ nearest to your Lord are not too proud to worship Him.
phrases.explanation: Concluding the surah with the supreme model of servitude, Allah declares that the noble angels stationed nearest to His Throne never disdain or grow too proud to worship their Lord in constant obedience. If the sinless angels nearest to the Throne never tire of worship, human beings have even less excuse for pride.

phrases.translation: They glorify Him. And to Him they prostrate
phrases.explanation: Those pure angels unceasingly exalt Allah above every imperfection and prostrate exclusively to Him, setting the example that believers follow at this first place of prostration in the Quran. Joining the angels in glorification and prostration brings the believer as near as possible to his Lord.
